#2221. Melvine Malard becomes Chelsea’s leading scorer as FOUR-goal start strengthens her claim to the No.9 role

Graduate Sports Journalist with a love for football.

Melvine Malard’s Chelsea goals are beginning to provide a persuasive answer to the club’s centre-forward question.

Her opener in Sunday’s 3-0 victory over West Ham took the summer signing to four competitive goals, making her Chelsea’s leading scorer this season.

That total comprises two goals in Champions League qualifying and two in the Women’s Super League.

The circumstances make those contributions particularly useful. Across three scoring appearances, Malard has broken a deadlock, restored a lead and helped Chelsea put difficult matches beyond their opponents.

Three of those goals arrived while Chelsea were level or protecting a one-goal advantage.

That gives the early return significance beyond its size. Malard has repeatedly contributed while there was still a contest to resolve.

Sunday provided the latest example. Chelsea had plenty of possession but needed somebody to turn an opening into a lead.

Turn and finish 💥Melvine Malard finishes for @ChelseaFCW 🔵#BarclaysWSL pic.twitter.com/eicBNrYMYk

According to Chelsea’s official match report, the Blues reached the half-hour mark without a shot on target despite having 64 per cent possession.

Sjoeke Nüsken created the breakthrough by winning possession and finding Malard.

The striker received the ball with her back to goal, held her position, turned and finished into the bottom corner.

It was an important demonstration of what she can offer centrally. Chelsea could find her under pressure and still get a shot away, rather than needing to release her into open space.

Nüsken’s contribution deserves equal recognition. Her pressing created the opportunity that Malard converted.

The sequence offers Bompastor something useful to build on: winning possession higher up the pitch and finding a forward capable of finishing before the opposition recover.

Malard’s first three Chelsea goals came as a substitute.

Her two-goal competitive debut against Real Sociedad immediately demonstrated that capacity to change a match.

Nüsken released her for the goal that restored Chelsea’s lead at 3-2. Ellie Carpenter subsequently supplied her second, extending the advantage to three goals.

The official account of that European victory records two different routes to goal: a run beyond the defence and a finish from a delivery across the box.

Against Birmingham, her alertness produced another valuable contribution. Malard punished hesitation over a backpass to score Chelsea’s second, eight minutes after coming on, as detailed in the club’s match report.

Those appearances give Bompastor flexibility. Malard has already influenced matches when introduced against tiring opponents, while West Ham supplied a scoring return from the starting role.

Chelsea signed Malard from Manchester United on a four-year contract, bringing her back together with a coach who first identified her potential at 14.

Bompastor later coached her in Lyon’s senior side. Their relationship therefore predates this summer’s recruitment by years.

Speaking when Chelsea announced her signing, Malard said:

“My objective is to become better every single day and to win trophies.”

Her next task is sustaining this contribution across a longer run of matches.

Competition remains productive. Aggie Beever-Jones replaced her at West Ham and supplied Maika Hamano’s late goal, giving Bompastor another reason to value both forwards.

Malard’s strongest argument is the range of situations she has already influenced. She has attacked space, finished crosses, punished hesitation and scored with a defender close behind her.

Four goals offer an encouraging early return. The variety behind them gives Chelsea something substantial to develop.

#2220. Supercomputer names the 3 EFL League One clubs that will get promoted

We're a quarter of the way through the EFL season, which gives us a good sample size to set more informed predictions about how the campaign will play out in all three divisions.

In League One, Huddersfield Town and Stockport County have been the two sides who have consistently impressed and deservedly led the way in the top two.

But below them, Luton Town have picked up a head of steam and some strong underlying numbers are starting to translate into results. They even took a lead at the Accu Stadium on Tuesday night against the league leaders, but were forced to settle for a draw.

Then, further down the table, Sheffield Wednesday have appointed Dave Challinor, and many believe that's the start of a resurgence at Hillsborough. Leicester City have the quality on the pitch and a system that's starting to settle under Russell Martin, and between them, the likes of Reading, Plymouth Argyle and Oxford United will be competitive, too.

So, it's all shaping up to be a very intriguing promotion race with a lot of sides who will believe they can go up, but who does AI think will be in the Championship next season? Football League World has taken a look to find out.

Winning the league, quite surprisingly in AI's eyes, are Oxford. The surprise mainly comes from the Yellows being nowhere near the top six in many critics' pre-season predictions.

There was logic to that reason, too, as Oxford weren't able to spend money and invest in the squad over the summer due to an embargo imposed on them after failing to comply with the EFL's SCMP regulations.

Football League World takes an in-depth look at the TEN most frustrating EFL Championship players right now

The Yellows were also going into the season with a novice head coach, too, after Matt Bloomfield was sacked in favour of ex-Arsenal and Wales midfielder Aaron Ramsey. Quite bluntly, no one really knew what to expect.

However, Ramsey has more than hit the ground running in the dugout, and Oxford's embargo, despite its frustrations, did mean that the vast majority of their squad that finished 22nd in the Championship and had a mid-table points tally under Bloomfield stuck around. The likes of Mark Harris, Michal Helik and Ciaron Brown have been great.

But also, Ramsey has done well to re-integrate some players many fans felt would never wear an Oxford shirt again. Siriki Dembele has been the main example of that, but Gatlin O'Donkor and Louie Sibley have contributed well, too.

There are questions about the overall depth at the Kassam. Teenagers Mo Missanga and Leo Snowdon are seeing more matchday squads than perhaps expected; albeit Missanga has been brilliant, but hopefully the embargo can be lifted in January, and Ramsey can bring in some reinforcements to help solidify what AI expects to be a title charge.

The current league leaders, Huddersfield, have been forecast by AI to slip from the summit but still secure automatic promotion.

That may be a disappointment right now, but given that the Terriers have failed to even finish in the top six in their two campaigns at third-tier level since their relegation from the Championship, it's a position they should more than take.

There's a clear argument that Huddersfield's squad is already Championship quality. It definitely is at the top end of the pitch. Joe Taylor and Derensili Sanches Fernandes already have 25 goals and assists between them through 14 games, which is quite frankly ridiculous.

But behind them, Cameron Humphreys has been one of the best midfielders in the division for a couple of years now, and it's mental that Huddersfield were able to keep him around for a second loan spell from Ipswich Town, and Archie Collins is more than thriving at a top-end League One club after leaving Peterborough United.

It says a lot that there are question marks over where Ryan Ledson fits in when he comes back from suspension, with the Terriers' club captain and someone with close to 200 Championship appearances patiently waiting on the sidelines.

And it's all being overseen by Martin Drury, an exciting, young manager whose attention to detail and demanding nature of a good performance can ruffle some feathers in the 'only results matter' camp, but it's more than working so far.

There may be a slight drop-off, but one that AI believes shouldn't be too detrimental to their promotion push.

After failing in the play-offs for the last two seasons, AI thinks that Stockport will finally get over the line and secure a second-tier return for the first time since the 2001/02 campaign.

There were some understandable concerns about the immediate future of the Hatters heading into this season, with influential CEO Simon Wilson and manager Dave Challinor moving on after the play-off final, but those have been dispelled very quickly.

There's an argument to be made that County are even better now under Jimmy McNulty than they were under Challinor, and that's no slight on the good work done at Edgeley Park over the previous five years.

They have so many different avenues of attack, whether that be patient, on the floor, working through the lines with Ollie Norwood and a reintegrated Lewis Bate in the pivots, or they can go long and hit Kyle Wootton, who remains one of the best target men strikers in the entire EFL, given how well he can hold the ball up and be a goal threat, too.

Do you agree with AI's promotion predictions in League One this season? Let us know in the comments.

Stockport can sometimes get caught out defensively. It took them a little while to get to grips with their new out-of-possession play at the start of the season, and Oxford did showcase how to beat their high line, once they finally stayed onside.

But any worries of them fading away after back-to-back third-placed finishes seem to have dissipated already, and AI feels that it could be third time's the charm in terms of them earning promotion, winning ahead of the likes of Plymouth, Reading, Sheffield Wednesday, Luton and Leicester.

#2219. Manchester United defence: Why Carrick must trust Yoro and Heaven

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United endured another embarrassing draw against 10-man Tottenham after failing to register their second win despite bringing in a plethora of players.

Manchester United invested heavily last season in their attacking options, bringing in Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha.

This season, they overhauled their midfield. United spent massively on Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos. Despite spending massively, they have failed to produce the control they would have expected in the midfield. The lack of control was evident in the recent Tottenham game, where Mainoo-Tielemans partnership failed to control the game collectively.

The midfield question was covered in our recent report as well, highlighting a lack of control and carried comments from Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp.

The bigger question is when United will strengthen their defence. As per our previous report as well, Manchester United are planning to overhaul their defence in the upcoming transfer windows.

United were heavily linked with several left backs but eventually failed to bring any one. The situation left Luke Shaw as the only senior option in the position, while Patrick Dorgu is used upfront by Michael Carrick.

Harry Amass is another option for Michael Carrick, but he is only here because of a failed transfer move. He has been rarely used at left back as Dalot and Mazraoui get the nod in the position ahead of him.

The situation at right-back isn’t all good either. Diogo Dalot is the first option there, but he rarely provides the assurance that puts Michael Carrick at ease. Noussair Mazraoui is the second choice at right-back, but his attacking numbers aren’t great either.

Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez form up United’s centre-back pairing while Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven are used all over the defensive line in rotation when needed. Yoro was used at right-back against Tottenham while Heaven arrived as left-back towards the end of the game.

Manchester United’s season hasn’t been defensively strong or anywhere near being good. They have conceded goals in all Premier League games and only kept one clean sheet against Sabah in the Champions League.

Lisandro Martinez has come under scrutiny after errors on four occasions. Against Ipswich Town, Manchester United won 5-2, but his error resulted in Ipswich’s second goal.

His own goal against Fulham gave away two points at Craven Cottage in the 1-1 draw. Another error led to Solanke’s goal against Tottenham, when he took his eyes off the ball.

His injury concerns are another aspect, and maybe Michael Carrick needs to make a decision.

Manchester United’s success depended heavily on youth over the years. When pundits questioned them, Sir Alex Ferguson gave them the chance to prove them wrong. Alan Hansen made the famous quote “You can’t win anything with kids” on the BBC’s Match of the Day on August 19, 1995. United did exactly that, played youth and went on to win everything.

Michael Carrick needs to do exactly that. He needs to trust youth and allow them to make mistakes. Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven arrived as massive potentials, but they haven’t been given the license to express themselves, without fearing for their places. Both the youngsters have rarely started together or in a stretch of games. It is maybe time for them to take their chances.

Michael Carrick needs to keep Harry Maguire as a senior experienced figure around them. There is no doubt over Martinez’s ability, but he is not the answer to United’s long-term problem. United need to blend youth with experience as their identity moving forward. Lisandro Martinez perhaps isn’t the answer to United’s problem.

A defensive revival expected in the upcoming transfer windows needs to happen now. It must happen with chances to the Youth. Michael Carrick needs to be brave enough and throw the youngsters in the mix. What it will bring is a long-term solution. They need to experience the errors and pressures that will shape them in football.

#2218. Danny Drinkwater on Chelsea move he ‘could never turn down’

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

The Danny Drinkwater Chelsea story still carries a sting. Five years at Stamford Bridge gave him plenty of time to think about how it all turned out, and his own verdict is not a happy one.

Drinkwater opened up in a Truth or Padel appearance alongside David Ornstein. He said the move was one he could never have turned down, even with the benefit of hindsight. “No, I don’t regret moving. I regret, in hindsight, how it’s turned out. I think I could never turn it down,” he said.

Strip away the headlines and the numbers alone tell an uncomfortable story. Drinkwater spent five years on Chelsea’s books. In that time he made just 23 appearances, according to the original interview report.

Do the maths and it barely comes to five games a year. That is a thin return for a central midfielder signed to compete for a first-team place. It is also the kind of record that rarely sits well at a club of Chelsea’s size and ambition.

Chelsea’s best attacking spells over a similar stretch of seasons look far more productive, as our striker rankings show. Set next to those numbers, Drinkwater’s five quiet years stand out even more starkly.

Five years. Twenty three games. These numbers alone explains why this transfer still gets talked about by Drinkwater, long after the headlines faded.

The numbers only tell part of the story. A string of incidents turned a quiet, underwhelming spell into something far more pointed.

Drinkwater had a training-ground bust-up while out on loan. He was also involved in an on-pitch brawl with Chelsea’s own under-23s side. Flashpoints between a first-team player and a development squad are rare at any club, let alone one with Chelsea’s standards.

Taken alone, either incident might have passed as a bad day. Taken together, it became harder to see Drinkwater simply as an unlucky squad player who could not catch a break.

The most serious moment came during his time at Aston Villa. Drinkwater headbutted team-mate Jota and was fined two weeks’ wages for it. He says the consequences at Chelsea did not stop there.

“They didn’t formally ban me, but I got removed from the first team building after the incident at Villa,” Drinkwater said.

One off-field incident, at another club, pushed him out of the manager’s day-to-day plans back home. No formal punishment at Chelsea followed. The effect was much the same.

Chelsea fans saw a similar breakdown of trust play out when Graham Potter struggled to win over the dressing room during another difficult Chelsea transition. Trust can break down fast once results or behaviour turn against the person at the centre of it.

Drinkwater’s comments matter beyond his own career. They are a reminder that saying yes to a big move does not guarantee it will work once a player walks through the door.

That tension has not gone away. Chelsea’s current transfer business, covered in our transfer watch, shows the club still weighing big calls on players whose futures depend on more than form alone.

Squad management under Xabi Alonso, assessed in our bomb squad verdict, raises a familiar issue. Players who fall outside a manager’s plans rarely find a quick way back in, whether the exile is formal or not.

Drinkwater never found his way back into Chelsea’s plans after the Villa incident. His account of the Danny Drinkwater Chelsea years stands as a blunt warning. A move that looks impossible to refuse can still become one of the hardest spells of a career.

#2217. Middlesbrough fans think Kim Hellberg got one thing wrong v Wrexham

Middlesbrough fell to their second defeat of the Championship season on Wednesday night, as Wrexham bounced back from consecutive defeats to pick up a vital three points at the Racecourse Ground.

In a game with very few chances, Phil Parkinson's side broke the deadlock with 20 minutes to go through George Thomason, and made sure the points were safe after Ollie Rathbone scored a second six minutes from time.

It's the first time that Middlesbrough have failed to score all season. Kim Hellberg's side have been electric going forward, led primarily by Will Lankshear, and it wasn't a coincidence that his absence after suffering a muscle issue led to Boro being a little less dangerous in front of goal.

However, it wasn't just the fact that Middlesbrough lined up with the likes of Kyle Joseph, Tommy Conway and David Strelec as the central nine at times on Wednesday night which frustrated Boro fans, as for the first time in quite a while, Hellberg himself wasn't without criticism.

Kim Hellberg is one of the more tactically fluid head coaches in the Championship today. He's comfortable deploying a back four or a back three, and spoke in his press conference last week about being happy operating with two strikers.

Unfortunately, the switch to a back three in possession and a back five out of it against Wrexham on Wednesday night has drawn quite a bit of criticism from Boro fans.

With Hellberg's side having a chance to extend their lead atop the table to four points last night against a Wrexham side who have underwhelmed this season and had lost their last two, the supporters were disappointed to see a perceived 'negative' lineup.

"Far too negative against a bang average side Kim. I hope you've learned from this? You know the score mate, sort it out. UTB!🇦🇹" one fan said on X in response to the Swede's post-match interview.

"5 at the back? More defensive against Moore? A team sat in the bottom half of the league, shambles Kim," another said.

Do you think Kim Hellberg got it wrong against Wrexham on Wednesday? Let us know in the comments.

Other fans accused Hellberg of "inviting Wrexham to give us a game," while others expressed frustration at setting up in a five "against a poor team." "He has to take responsibility for the formation and selections!" was also among the comments.

"Lost for words Kim? Poor team selection and formation tonight. Never play with a back 3 again," was said bluntly. Evidently, the majority of Middlesbrough fans are hoping Hellberg reverts to a back four on Saturday at Watford.

Ultimately, while Wrexham haven't enjoyed the start to the season that many expected they would have, Phil Parkinson's side is still full of talented players who can hurt any team on a good day.

This one can be chalked up to a sub-par performance from a Middlesbrough side and a bit of a better one from a Wrexham perspective, and the fact that Boro are still sitting top of the division regardless, just shows how strong they have been to start the season.

No league champion goes the whole campaign without losing, and those at the Riverside will be hoping that this is just a mere bump in the road en route to a Premier League return.

Kim Hellberg's side are in action at Vicarage Road on Saturday as they take on Watford in the final game before the November international break.

#2215. Keira Walsh adds another Chelsea weapon as former Arsenal target scores THIRD goal of the season

Graduate Sports Journalist with a love for football.

Keira Walsh is giving Chelsea opponents another decision to make: protect the penalty area or step out to stop her shooting.

Her goal in Sunday’s 3-0 victory at West Ham took her to three for the season across all competitions. Each has come from outside the box.

For a player whose passing helps organise Chelsea’s attacks, that threat adds another way to influence matches. Recent performances show her contributing both to the construction of chances and their finish.

Against Sociedad, Walsh struck from distance after a corner, helping Chelsea complete their passage into the Champions League’s league phase.

The club’s account of that qualifying victory describes a tight encounter in which clear opportunities were limited.

At Manchester United, Lucy Bronze found her near the edge of the box and Walsh drove her finish into the bottom corner.

She also supplied Lauren James’ goal that afternoon, as Chelsea’s match report records. It was a useful illustration of the choices she offers: attempt the finish herself or release somebody closer to goal.

West Ham provided another example of that balance.

Walsh had already struck the post before Alyssa Thompson carried the ball in from the left and found Wieke Kaptein. Kaptein moved it on to Walsh, whose finish gave Chelsea breathing space.

The official report also records an earlier Walsh run down the channel and delivery towards Sjoeke Nüsken.

Her involvement therefore extended beyond waiting for opportunities to shoot. She helped Chelsea approach the penalty area from different positions.

There was a similar reward against Arsenal a week earlier. Walsh’s saved effort fell to Thompson for the only goal, as covered in our report of Chelsea’s derby victory.

That sequence illustrates why a dangerous shot can matter even when the goalkeeper stops it. Chelsea had a runner ready to attack the rebound.

Our assessment is that Walsh’s shooting gives defenders an additional problem. Closing her down can open a passing route; allowing her time leaves the goalkeeper exposed to a player already finding her range.

Walsh has also explained why she feels comfortable alongside Potter.

Speaking after the Arsenal victory in an interview published by Chelsea, she said:

“Lexi is really intelligent. She makes me feel really comfortable when I’m playing next to her.”

Her wider assessment emphasised collective responsibility, with team-mates covering for each other and working to make Chelsea harder to beat.

That matters when assessing midfield influence. Walsh’s freedom to help an attack depends partly on the positioning and decisions of those around her.

Potter subsequently started alongside her in Chelsea’s confirmed team against Lyon, giving their partnership another demanding European assignment.

The encouraging feature is the trust Walsh describes. Bompastor has an experienced organiser working with a younger midfielder whose reading of the game she clearly values.

BBC Sport reported that Barcelona rejected Arsenal’s bid for Walsh in September 2024.

Chelsea completed her signing in January 2025 on a four-and-a-half-year contract. Her official club profile outlines the technical quality and ability to dictate tempo that underpinned that recruitment.

Those qualities remain central to her value. Three early goals strengthen the attacking contribution around them, without establishing that she has changed position or should abandon her deeper responsibilities.

For Bompastor, the opportunity is to preserve that balance: Walsh helping Chelsea progress through midfield, supporting those around her and recognising when the space opens for a finish.

#2213. Michael Chopra drops Cardiff City exit verdict on ‘unbelievable’ star

Former Cardiff City cult hero Michael Chopra has issued a claim on the form of Jack Moylan, whose fine start to life at the Cardiff City Stadium continued with a first-half hat-trick in the 3-3 draw with West Ham United.

Much of the pre-match discourse in South Wales was on Scott Parker's first game in charge of the Hammers, but it seemed as though the Bluebirds were going to make it three successive losses for them through Moylan's individual brilliance.

The Republic of Ireland international opened the scoring with a stunning strike from distance after 11 minutes, before netting twice more before the interval.

After drawing a foul from Morato, Moylan beat Mads Hermansen from the penalty spot before glancing home his hat-trick and second in as many minutes just six minutes before half-time.

Ultimately, West Ham staged a thrilling fightback and were level on 82 minutes through goals from Divine Mukasa, Arne Engels and Max Kilman, but that took nothing away from the stunning form Moylan continues to demonstrate in South Wales.

Who are the most clutch players in the Championship that could whip in a last-minute set piece worldie?

Moylan arrived in the Welsh capital in August from fellow Championship newcomers, Lincoln City, despite only signing fresh terms at the ProAmpac Stadium six months ago.

After scoring 11 times in 31 League One appearances for last season's third tier winners, the attacking midfielder is already the joint-second-highest goal-getter in the Championship, with his treble against the Irons seeing him match Andri Gudjohnsen's tally of nine for Blackburn Rovers.

The six-time international has posted three further assists as Cardiff sit 18th on 15 points, and Chopra, who scored 63 times in 159 appearances, had this to say on the 25-year-old.

"Said it a couple months ago @JackMoylan8 is some player," the former striker posted on X. "A first half hat trick unbelievable.

"@CardiffCityFC going to have a fight to keep hold of him in January," he added.

Many of Barry-Murphy's squad have earned praise in recent times for the way in which they have performed, with some still in the early stages of their highly promising careers.

At 25, there is also more room for Moylan to enhance his potential, which has only grown through his recent performances, and unsurprisingly, many Cardiff fans share Chopra's sentiment.

"I'm worried like you Michael he has come in and really lifted the club up players and fans we have really got to try and hold on to him our season will have a real bad hit if he goes," said one Bluebirds supporter.

Another responded: "No it isn’t mate cmon ! Only been here a couple months! End of season maybe but not January!"

However, not all were of this opinion, with another social media comment reading: "January is going to be a chance to see how the board see us when the bids for Moylan come in."

"Difference between Cardiff pushing for top half and being dragged into a relegation battle. Nobody else in that team has that level of quality in front of goal," was another verdict of Moylan's immediate impact.

Given Chopra's cult hero status at Cardiff, it was high praise that one Cardiff fan wrote: "Nearly, but not quite, as good as you!," in response to the former striker's opinion.

Cardiff fans, do you fear a sudden January exit for Jack Moylan? Comment below!

Moylan's performances have also been noted by supporters of other clubs, with a Birmingham City fan adding: "No chance he doesn’t get a prem move in January, bloke is class."

Few would be surprised if Moylan's current form perks the interest of clubs ahead of the winter window, although Cardiff fans will be hoping they avoid a quick sale of the playmaker.

However, the Bluebirds would still hold significant power in negotiations after agreeing a four-year deal with the Dubliner, whilst those associated with Lincoln are hoping that a sell-on clause was inserted in his sale.

At present, Moylan is proving to be the difference-maker for Barry-Murphy's side, and many will be expecting him to feature again in Heimir Hallgrímsson's Ireland plans against Austria and Kosovo next week.

#2212. Why must Manchester United move beyond the Glazers?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

The Glazers took control of Manchester United in 2005. That takeover has since caused so many disruptions and protests by the fans over massive debts and insufficient backing of the team in the transfer market, despite successful periods in the Premier League and Europe.

Now Manchester United need to think about who should control the club in the future. Laurie Whitwell has now shared his views on why Manchester United need an ownership change. He simply wants the Glazers gone from Old Trafford. However, he also recognizes that replacing the current ownership doesn’t automatically mean things will improve for United.

The journalist believes the change in ownership has had a lasting effect on United, with the club still feeling its consequences today. A fresh start might be welcome, but the identity of the next owners would matter just as much as the departure of the existing ones.

“Personally, I would like to see the Glazers gone from Manchester United,” Laurie Whitwell said on The Rest is Football podcast with Gary Lineker.

“That change, you know, just really affected and still impacts United now.”

The desire for different ownership is one thing, but finding people capable of taking the club forward is another.

Whitwell admitted there is no perfect answer when it comes to who should take charge.

That leaves United facing a difficult choice. A sale could offer the chance to change how the club is run, but simply bringing in a new owner would not guarantee better decisions or a brighter future.

Whitwell also raised the idea of United supporters having a greater say in the club’s ownership and decisions, much like the Barcelona model where fans own the club itself. However, he highlighted that the Barcelona model isn’t ideal either and has its own shortcomings.

Changing the names at the top would only be one part of the change. The club would also need an ownership structure capable of making sound decisions and providing a direction.

The issue of ownership goes beyond whether the Glazers should stay or leave. Manchester United needs to find the right people and the right model to secure the club’s future. Getting that decision wrong could leave them facing the same circus the fans are enduring under the Glazers.

Chelsea target Alex Scott has withdrawn from England duty with an injury that threatens his involvement in Bournemouth’s visit to Stamford Bridge on Saturday.

England confirmed on Monday morning that Scott had returned to his club for further assessment and would miss Tuesday’s Nations League match against Czechia.

Sky Sports reports a tendon injury, with initial indications suggesting an absence of several weeks. Further scans are planned.

Bournemouth face Chelsea on 10 October, the first game in the Blues’ run of fixtures after the international break.

Thomas Tuchel said England had received assurances about his fitness before the match.

England’s announcement did not specify a recovery period. Bournemouth’s assessment will determine the extent of the injury and clarify his availability for Saturday.

#2210. Spurs will be surprised but Leicester's won't by Oliver Skipp at Charlton

Having shone when coming through the academy at Tottenham Hotspur and then experienced a bright start to his career in the EFL, Oliver Skipp is again struggling this season, now at Charlton Athletic after a tough time of it at Leicester City.

Following their promotion back to the Championship via the 2024-25 League One play-offs, Charlton have looked to assert themselves as a part of the furniture again in the second-tier, under the management of Nathan Jones.

A young squad under Jones as they gained promotion, Charlton did have a fair bit of experience dotted around their squad but, as ever with a team heading into a campaign seeking to avoid ‘second season syndrome’, they have again sought to add more pedigree to their squad.

That may well have even been with a view to kicking on into the middle-of-the-table and, albeit as an outsider, looked at the top eight and the expanded play-off spots to eight teams in the Championship this season.

One player that was brought in with good pedigree to provide extra quality in the middle of the park was Oliver Skipp – but the 26-year-old is enduring another struggle this season down at The Valley.

Over the summer, Charlton added a fair bit of experience to the middle of the park with the signing of Nathaniel Chalobah on a free transfer from Sheffield Wednesday and Timothy Ouma from Slavia Prague.

Both defensive midfielders, it was somewhat surprising that The Addicks then signed Oliver Skipp on loan from Leicester City on the final day of the campaign – albeit in a Nathan Jones-coached side, perhaps you can’t have too many conservative and defensive-minded midfielders.

Skipp, Ouma and Chalobah joined a squad that already boasted other key midfielders such as Conor Coventry, Greg Docherty and the slightly more advanced Sonny Carey, while the versatile Joe Rankin-Costello is also capable of playing in a central midfield role.

Whether it be a 4-2-3-1 system or even a three-at-the-back with either one or two so-called ‘number tens’; there tends to only be room for two out and out box-to-box or defensive central midfielders – and with the quality Skipp has previously shown and the experience he already has in his mid-20’s; Skipp was viewed as a floor-raising addition to a Charlton side that had won their opening three games of the campaign before his arrival.

However, Charlton have since gone on a ten-match winless run of form after the arrival of Skipp and his own individual performance have perhaps been reflective of the malaise and regression of the team as a whole.

A look at seven clubs who should consider trying to sign former Tottenham Hotspur and England man Dele Alli.

The former England U21 international came into the side immediately and played the full 90 minutes as Charlton endured their first loss of the season – a 4-0 hammering at the hands of Stoke City.

He has gone on to start seven of the next eight matches, too, only not involved against Norwich City after being hooked at half-time in a 2-0 defeat to Watford a week earlier.

He came back into the eleven against Middlesbrough but found himself in a midfield that was completely overrun by the league leaders in a 3-0 defeat at the Riverside Stadium in that one.

Keeping out Coventry in midfield, as well as even Chalobah, who had started life in South London well, being moved to the periphery of things seems now to be a surprising inevitability for Skipp.

Once a metronomic figure in terms of his passing and tempo setting when coming through Tottenham youth teams and then on loan at Norwich; Skipp has badly struggled to adapt to the more conservative nature of Jones’ style.

Skipp has remained tidy enough on the ball with an 83.1% pass success rate but he is averaging too few passes per game and allowing games to pass him by, averaging more than 12 passes per 90 fewer than Conor Coventry, as an example.

Previously better known for his ability on the ball, it is his defensive work that has been his more impressive suit thus far this season but, with ball-winners such as Chalobah at the club, more quality was to be expected of the Leicester loanee.

That quality was shown when coming through at Spurs as he made the fringes of the first-team picture in North London and even began to emerge with more regular minutes when coached by Antonio Conte – who he once suggested he could help become a ‘top midfielder’.

His breakthrough into more regular minutes at Spurs had come after an extremely impressive loan stint at Norwich during the 2020-21 campaign – named in the PFA Team of the Year for the second division that season as The Canaries won the Championship title under Daniel Farke.

That season, Skipp was that metronome in Norwich’s proactive and entertaining side, averaging 51.5 passes per game with an 88% pass success rate – dwarfing his figures at Charlton so far this season and highlighting his drop off.

That drop off being seen by Charlton supporters this season may come as a surprise to Spurs and Norwich supporters but it won’t be much of a shock for Leicester fans.

Purchased by The Foxes in the summer of 2024 for a fee believed to be in the region of £20 million, following Leicester’s Championship title-winning campaign under Enzo Maresca, Skipp linked up with Steve Cooper at the King Power Stadium.

A good coach but a pragmatic one, the passing and ability to retain possession that had been qualities of Skipp weren’t necessarily going to be used too much for a Cooper-led relegation battler.

However, his fierceness in the tackle and general industry also diminished in a Leicester squad that succumbed to back-to-back relegations from the Premier League and into League One.

Perhaps a very good example of Leicester’s issues in the last half a decade, being a big money signing brought in without too much sense in terms of exactly what they wanted; Skipp badly struggled at the King Power Stadium.

Having been one of the best players in the Championship and then someone seemingly coming close to England recognition in the years before his arrival at Leicester; a loss of confidence and inability to rediscover his quality on the ball led to Skipp sticking out as a fairly hapless figure in Leicester’s badly underperforming side.

Brought in for such a big fee, he managed just ten starts in his debut campaign as they were relegated from the Premier League before being a peripheral figure in the opening few months of last season.

Skipp became a key man for a Leicester side that became enemies of the fanbase and his failure to rediscover any sort of form at Charlton thus far will not come as much of a surprise to Foxes supporters.

#2209. Alfred Johansson issues major style warning to his Motherwell side

Motherwell manager Alfred Johansson believes they will need to develop different edges to their game as opponents catch up with their passing style.

Well are second only to Celtic in attempted passes and passing accuracy in the William Hill Premiership this season as they continue the brand of football introduced by Johansson’s predecessor, Jens Berthel Askou, last summer.

But other teams are now catching on after the success Motherwell and Falkirk had last season in finishing in the top six.

Johansson cited recent statistics that showed passes per Premiership game had increased by more than 100 to close to 900 from four seasons ago to this campaign, while passing accuracy was up from 74 per cent to more than 80 per cent and long passes had reduced by around a quarter over the same period.

“I saw some statistics a couple of weeks ago, how much higher the amount of passes in the Scottish football games are this season, compared only with last season,” Johansson said.

“There was also a comparison over a five-year period, and the amount of passes has increased a lot. And it was also a big step from last season to how this season has started.

“The game is moving in that direction, which I guess is natural. I mean, that’s how the trend has been in the rest of European football for quite some time.”

Johansson’s opponent on Saturday, Jim Goodwin, admitted last season that he would aspire to play the sort of football that Askou delivered and his new-look midfield trio of Dylan Tait, Lyall Cameron and Zidane Iqbal have helped adapt their style of play.

United are unbeaten in six matches since losing at Fir Park while Motherwell’s 1-0 win over St Mirren last weekend was their first in eight games.

Johansson senses that Motherwell’s style of play will not give them an inherent advantage.

“It was very different from many of the other teams (last season) and that then gave Motherwell an edge because they were very early,” the Swede said.

“Whereas this season, it’s more teams trying to, maybe not play in the exact same way, but at least have more passes than they had in the past.

“So if that is the case, that’s not going to be the one thing that’s going to be the difference between the teams.

“So I guess that style of play will not be the thing that separates the winner from loser. I think you’re going to have to be finding an edge elsewhere for how good you are with and without the ball.

“You need to be good on your basics. Making minor adaptations to an opponent is always going to be there, but it’s going to be minor changes.”

#2208. Fabrizio Romano shares latest on Martinez contract after explosive rant

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

The Argentinian defender has also apologized to the United higher ups as well over his comments, as shared by Fabrizio Romano.

Lisandro Martinez has held discussions with Jason Wilcox and Michael Carrick after speaking out following United’s 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid.

Martinez had questioned whether Carrick was backed enough in the summer and suggested the club needed changes.

Fabrizio Romano has now confirmed that United consider the matter resolved for now and expect Martinez to remain available for selection.

Speaking about the situation on his YouTube channel, as quoted by Football 365, Romano explained why Martinez’s comments caused concern inside the club.

“He spoke very strongly after the game against Atletico Madrid, which Man Utd lost. It was a very negative moment for the Red Devils. We know that Licha was very strong in his comments. He said that Michael Carrick was not backed enough during the summer transfer window.”

Romano added that Martinez had spoken directly to those at the club after the incident.

“Licha apologised to Man Utd as a club. He spoke to the directors, he spoke to Jason Wilcox, and he spoke to Michael Carrick, who was also involved in this conversation.”

“So, the underlying message remains the same. Lisandro is apologising for the way he expressed himself after a game during a difficult moment for Man Utd, but there was a discussion about the substance of what he said.”

Romano also revealed that United had imposed a financial penalty on the centre-back. However, the punishment does not appear to involve removing him from the squad.

“According to the information available tonight, Lisandro Martinez has been fined.”

He added that Martinez is expected to return to the squad as normal, with the fine considered sufficient punishment for the incident.

“The internal discussion also helped to resolve all the issues. For Man Utd, the case is closed.”

That should bring some immediate clarity to the situation, although questions remain about how the episode could affect Martinez’s longer-term position at Old Trafford.

Romano also pointed towards Martinez’s contract, which expires next summer, with United holding an option to extend it.

“So, let’s see what is going to happen there. For sure, this is the kind of situation that will have an impact on the situation surrounding Lisandro, but we have to see what happens next in terms of future transfers and everything else.”

Lisandro Martinez could return to Manchester United’s starting line-up against Leeds United this weekend, with the defender reportedly available for selection after the controversy surrounding his comments about the club’s summer transfer business.

#2203. Birmingham City told to strike Nottingham Forest transfer for 95-cap international star

Birmingham City's impressive start to the season has got many fans at St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park dreaming of a return to the Premier League for the first time since 2011.

Chris Davies' side have only lost two of their first 14 matches of the Championship season, winning four of their last five and scoring 14 goals in the process.

Tuesday's controlled 3-0 win over Millwall saw Birmingham reach the automatic promotion places for just over 24 hours, before they were knocked down to third for the time being after Wolves' win at Bristol City.

Such a strong start wasn't exactly forecast by many in this part of the Second City at the beginning of the season, as it was argued that the squad was left short in certain areas.

However, given the well-documented ambitions of American investors, Knighthead Capital Management, many are now debating what activity will be conducted in the winter window if Blues are still among the promotion contenders.

With Birmingham's forward department currently made up of August Priske, Jay Stansfield, Luis Vazquez and Marvin Ducksch, it has been questioned what changes will be made going forward.

Priske has already netted six times this season whilst Stansfield has now firmly aclimatised to playing as a 'number 10', whilst exit talk continues to surround Ducksch after a failed summer departure to Valencia, and Vazquez is yet to convince the majority of supporters.

As such, it was recently debated by Blues YouTuber, Tommy Kelsall, whether a reunion for Chris Wood, who scored 11 times in 29 appearances on loan in the 2011/12 season under Chris Hughton, makes sense, given his similarities with Priske, but also the experience under his belt.

The in-form striker was absent from Tuesday's dominant success over Millwall

Wood has only made two Premier League starts under Oliver Glasner at Nottingham Forest this season, having seen his 2025/26 campaign blighted by a knee injury.

Beforehand, the 95-time New Zealand international scored 20 times as the Reds secured European football in 2024/25, and his record of 170 strikes in the top two divisions is indisputable.

With his contract at the City Ground up next June, Football League World's Birmingham City fan pundit, Jason Moore, believes the 34-year-old would be a great option for Davies to call upon.

"I don't mind the shout," Moore told FLW.

"People might say he's aging, but he's, again, a proven Premier League striker. He's done a decent job in the Premier League.

"He's not pacey. But, I don't think that's his game and he'd probably be, like that tweet says, a like-for-like for August Priske in the way we play, so I'd be all up for it.

"You know he's going to work hard, he'd take that pressure off Priske playing every single game, and he's a miles better replacement than Luis Vazquez.

"If you can look at Chris Wood and if he's not playing at Forest, then I'd be all for it. If we could pull that off, that's a great shout. Him or Che (Adams), I'd be all up for it."

Blues fans, should Chris Davies attempt to sign Chris Wood in January? Comment below!

"I'd narrowly favour Che for his pace, but I'd be more than happy with Chris Wood if Che wasn't available. Both are excellent options."

Having a focal point in attack such as Priske has allowed Birmingham to source goals from across Davies' squad, and whilst the Dane has become a feared striker this term, Wood's experience would certainly aid a promotion bid.

Like Priske, he has the ability to bring fellow attackers into the game and make their own deep runs into the box and create chances, whilst also having a poacher's instinct despite not being particularly fast.

If Birmingham were also to end their Premier League exile, then a player of such calibre would also be worth retaining, given Wood's extensive record in both divisions.

The nature of the Championship schedule also means that the forward is likely to source more minutes in the West Midlands than he currently is in the East.

#2200. Fleetwood 1-1 Arsenal (5-3 penalties): Gunners knocked out of Carabao Cup as Max Dowman is sent off

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal suffered a stunning Carabao Cup exit. They lost on penalties to League Two side Fleetwood Town 5-3 in the fourth round at Highbury Stadium. A 1-1 draw meant Arsenal had to go to penalties. Teenager Max Dowman was sent off five minutes from the end of the game.

Fleetwood, in 18th place in League Two, took an early lead, but Viktor Gyokeres scored his first goal of the season to bring them level. However, neither team could find a winning goal. Fleetwood held their composure to win the penalty shootout after Bruno Guimaraes missed his spot-kick. The game was also paused for two minutes due to a drone flying around the ground.

Despite a heavy rotation by Mikel Arteta, Kai Havertz, Gyokeres, Martin Zubimendi, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Jurrien Timber all started. Martin Odegaard and Ben White were brought on during the half-time break, followed by Guimaraes, Ezri Konsa and Eberechi Eze. But overall the Evening Standard said Arsenal put in an “incredibly bad performance” over the course of the 90 minutes.

Dowman, 16, had been among Arsenal’s better players, creating chances for Havertz and Timber with dangerous crosses. He was shown a straight red card after reacting angrily to a heavy challenge from Harrison Neal and kicking out at the defender, though the force was minimal. It was his second red card this month, after a dismissal for the England Under-19s.

As Dowman walked off, Arteta was seen leaning towards him and delivering furious words. Asked what he said, the Arsenal manager told BBC Radio 5 Live it was “something that we discussed already before the match”. Suggesting the teenager had been warned to expect rough treatment. Arteta said he had not seen the red card back and that the referee’s decision stood. Sky Sports pundit Paul Merson was critical of how the Arsenal boss reacted to Dowman.

Arteta congratulated Fleetwood Town on the atmosphere they created. He said he could not fault his players’ attitude and intensity, with 11 men or 10. “When we create the volume of shots and chances we did, you have to score three, four or five,” he said. He added that even with ten men Arsenal had three big chances.

He called the unpredictability of cup football part of English football’s history, saying Arsenal were “extremely sad” to be on the wrong side of it.

Several squad members were absent. Riccardo Calafiori was out, and Noni Madueke had an ankle problem. Declan Rice was substituted in the previous game because of a concern.

Arsenal’s Carabao Cup dream of a first League Cup win since 1993 is over. Attention now turns to a huge Premier League trip to Anfield to face Liverpool on Sunday. Fleetwood, meanwhile, can celebrate a famous giant-killing and wait for the quarter-final draw.

Sheffield United, despite a difficult summer transfer window, have bounced back with aplomb and cannot be ruled out of a play-off spot this season, and one player will be crucial to those efforts.

Sheffield United underwent a difficult summer window, with each of Andre Brooks, Gustavo Hamer, and Callum O'Hare leaving the club to bring in some much-needed funds, as loans and free transfers were heavily relied upon as a means to bring in recruits.

Through AI, we'll rank the top 25 most intimidating football stadiums in British football, but which stadium comes out on top?

Sydie Peck has been in the headlines as of late for his surprising first-half hat-trick against Preston North End in midweek, but the midfielder's displays throughout this campaign deserve more recognition.

Coming through the Arsenal academy before joining the Blades in 2021, the 22-year-old has made over a century of appearances for the South Yorkshire outfit across all competitions since, and has gone on to become one of the first names on the team sheet under Chris Wilder in recent years.

A regular in the England youth setup, Peck is bound for the Premier League at some stage of his career, and with four goals and two assists in 14 Championship games from midfield already this season, it's no surprise January interest in the midfielder is expected.

Football League World's Sheffield United fan pundit, Jimmy from Blades Ramble, has shared their thoughts on whether Peck will attract interest from elsewhere in the near future, and if so, how much the Blades should demand for the midfielder.

Jimmy said: "I fully expect interest in Sydie Peck in January. He's a good player, and I think Chris Wilder noted in his post-match interview that he needed to add goals to his game, and he started to do that.

"So a hat-trick, very impressive, but really his overall game has improved, and I definitely think he has the ability to become a Premier League player.

"I would prefer it if he stayed under the radar a little bit and stayed with Sheffield United. What I do think, though, is, now that there's no longer a need to sell at Bramall Lane, if Sydie Peck does get an offer that we find too good to refuse, then I think Wilder will be given a lot of the funds to strengthen the squad.

"We've been in this position before when we sold David Brooks, and we brought in players like John Egan and Ollie Norwood. But what is that price? I think it's at least £15 million. When you look at some of the prices that players are going for at this level now, he's an England U21 international who just scored a hat-trick in the Championship; at least £15 million. I'd be holding out for £20 million."

Do you agree with Jimmy's take on Sydie Peck? How much do you think Sheffield United should be commanding for the midfielder if interest were to arrive as early as January? Share your thoughts below!

Having been forced to part ways with Brooks, Hamer, and O'Hare in the summer, Sheffield United and their head coach Chris Wilder will have little intention of losing any other stars anytime soon.

Peck is certainly one of their prized assets right now, and under contract until the summer of 2028, are under no immediate pressure to cash in, although, a decision on his future must be made sooner rather than later.

The England youth international's ceiling is extraordinarily high, and Sheffield United will be hoping to be the continued beneficiaries of his services for years to come, as time will tell exactly how this saga plays out.

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal Women face Benfica at Meadow Park tonight, and as they prepare to enter a tough clash in the UEFA Women’s Champions League, head coach Renée Slegers has called for ‘grit and fight’ from her players. The match kicks off at 8pm in Borehamwood and will be available to watch live on Disney+ for UK fans.

Arsenal come into the match on the back of a 2-1 north London derby win at Tottenham. The team sit fifth in the European league with four points, having won 1-0 at home against HB Koge and drawn 2-2 at Paris FC. Benfica are currently sitting in tenth place but will overtake them if they win.

Slegers said the main factor behind Arsenal’s derby win was intensity. “It was a really intense game. We had to fight for it. We scored first, and we came back, so that’s what makes me really proud. Now we have to make sure we follow that up,” she said at London Colney on Tuesday.

Kim Little returns to the squad. Slegers confirmed that Katie Reid and Michelle Agyemang will not be back in time, while Frida Maanum is progressing, but the game comes too soon.

Taylor Hinds was a player of the match contender at Tottenham, playing a full 90 minutes for only the second time this season. Alongside Steph Catley, she linked up well on the left. Slegers has not named the same starting XI in back-to-back games this season, though, and said Arsenal will need “sharpness, quality and injections” late on against Benfica.

The referee is Ivana Projkovska of North Macedonia, who was among the officials for the 2025 Champions League final, when Arsenal beat Barcelona 1-0 in Lisbon.

Benfica have won all four of their Campeonato Nacional Feminino games as they look to retain their title, conceding once, in Saturday’s 4-1 win over Sporting CP. In Europe, Ivan Baptista’s side won 2-1 at Juventus before losing 3-0 at home to Bayern Munich. They have made more interceptions than any other team in this season’s competition, with 33, while Arsenal have made only 13.

Slegers expects a physical, compact opponent, similar in some ways to the derby, though with some changes in personnel since last season, when Arsenal won 2-0 at the Estadio da Luz through Beth Mead and Alessia Russo. Baptista said being seen as favourites means little to him and that his team will cause Arsenal difficulties again.

The record favours the hosts. Arsenal have won 10 of their last 13 home league-phase games in the competition, including the last three, while Benfica have won only three of their last 15 away matches in the tournament.

Slegers admitted the domestic start has been tough but said it is too early to judge and that Arsenal are proud to be back on the Champions League stage. Last season they finished fifth in the league phase before reaching the semi-finals.

Scott Parker’s start to life as West Ham head coach got off to a thrilling start.

The Hammers drew 3-3 against Cardiff City on Wednesday night in his first game in the dugout, with the team coming from 3-0 behind to secure a point on the road.

Goals from Divine Mukasa, Arne Engels and Max Kilman sealed an exciting comeback in the second half, with the London outfit hoping that they can compete for automatic promotion this season.

But Parker’s first game as manager showed that there is perhaps more work to be done at the London Stadium than initially thought.

The first issue that Parker may have to address as the new West Ham boss is the underwhelming form of summer arrival Manor Solomon.

The winger was brought in with the expectation that he could power the team to promotion, much like he did at Leeds United in 2024/25, where he contributed 10 goals and 12 assists in 39 Championship appearances.

Should Scott Parker drop Manor Solomon? Comment your opinion below

But his form has been inconsistent at the London Stadium so far, and another underwhelming performance on Wednesday night led to him being hauled off after 69 minutes.

While he managed to complete 13 of his 15 attempted passes, the overall total matches that of someone quite uninvolved in the game, and he also failed to create a chance or take a clear shot at goal, leading to a deserved substitution (all stats from Fotmob).

Edvin Austbo was chosen to replace Solomon for the final 20 minutes against Cardiff, making his 10th appearance in the league this season.

This was the eighth time he came off the bench, and his lively performance helped the team in their comeback from 3-0 down.

West Ham United considered the potential appointment of former Tottenham Hotspur and Liverpool coach Johnny Heitinga before deciding on Scott Parker

The Norwegian already has as many goals and assists as Solomon so far this campaign, despite playing only 347 minutes compared to 1,003.

Austbo hasn’t had an extended run in the team, which impacts how we can judge him, but his appearances so far have shown a lot of promise.

The winger has an expected assists (xA) per 90 of 0.53, creating 0.53 big chances per 90.

He also has 1.32 successful crosses each game at a success rate of 35.7 per cent, which makes him a dangerous threat in the final third, all while also taking 2.63 shots each game himself.

If he can replicate these kinds of performances over a series of starts in the coming weeks, then Parker will have no choice but to keep him in the lineup going forward over Solomon.

West Ham’s rivals Tottenham Hotspur signed Solomon in 2023, but he struggled for game time under various managers at the London outfit, which led to loan spells at Leeds, Villarreal and Fiorentina.

But the Hammers committed to a £5 million deal to sign the winger despite his lack of impact at Spurs.

Given the question marks over his quality now, the Premier League side have had the last laugh on their rival.

Parker dropping him to the bench would be the ultimate vindication for Spurs’ decision to cash in on the forward last summer.

#2191. Rob Edwards backed to replace John Eustace at Derby County - but Middlesbrough 'concern' raised

It has been a nightmare start to the season for Derby County in the Championship.

After missing out on the play-offs on the final day of last season, many expected Derby to mount another promotion push this time around, but it has certainly not worked out that way.

It was another disastrous night for Derby as they were beaten 4-0 by Norwich City at Pride Park on Tuesday night, with goals from Anthony Musaba, Paris Maghoma, Darlin Yongwa and Jovon Makama sealing an emphatic victory for the Canaries.

The Rams' latest defeat extended their winless run to 10 games, and while they remain 23rd in the Championship table, they are now seven points from safety after winning just one of their opening 14 matches.

Despite increasing numbers of supporters calling for head coach John Eustace to be sacked, the 47-year-old will be in charge for the visit of Bolton Wanderers on Friday night, but with the November international break looming, he will be desperate for a result against the 17th-placed Trotters.

Should Derby part company with Eustace, one name that has been suggested as a potential replacement is Rob Edwards, who has been out of work since leaving Wolverhampton Wanderers in June following their relegation from the Premier League.

Edwards' most notable achievement came when he led Luton Town to promotion to the top flight via the play-offs in 2023, while he has also had spells with the likes of Forest Green Rovers, Watford and Middlesbrough, and he has been linked with a number of Championship clubs this season, including Southampton, Burnley and Wrexham.

When asked for his thoughts on the possible appointment of Edwards, FLW's Derby County fan pundit Shaun Woodward said that he would be happy to see the 43-year-old replace Eustace, but he admitted that he has concerns about his lack of loyalty after he walked away from Middlesbrough after just 16 games in charge to join Wolves last November.

"Forget Rob Edwards, I'd probably take Rob Earnshaw right now with the way things are going at Derby," Shaun told FLW.

"John Eustace has lost the dressing room, he sounds like a defeated man when he's doing his interviews post-match.

"We're shipping goals at an alarming rate, we're not looking like we're going to score, there's no fight in the team.

"They all look like they're out for themselves, they're hiding, it's a horrid, horrid time to be a Derby fan right now.

"We desperately need a change of manager.

"Rob Edwards has got experience of getting promotion out of this league at Luton, he did well in the Premier League as well with limited resources.

"My only problem with him is when he was at Middlesbrough and seemingly had a good thing going there, his head was turned, and he left to go to Wolves, which worries me.

"We've had quite a few managers over the years that have done well at Derby, and then a bigger club has come looking and they've left.

"That worries me with Rob Edwards, would he do the same again?

"Let's say he got us up the table this season, next season he gets us promoted or in and around it, and then another club comes looking and he leaves us.

"We want stability at the club, so that's my only concern with Edwards, but I would take him right now because something has to change.

While Edwards had a strong connection to Wolves, his decision to leave Middlesbrough while they were second in the Championship to take over at a club that looked doomed to relegation from the Premier League was questionable, and it will be a red flag in the minds of prospective employers.

With the club currently sitting seven points from safety, it seems Derby could be involved in a battle for survival this season, and it would be a risk for them to appoint a manager who has two relegations on his CV with Luton and Wolves, even if there are mitigating circumstances for those failures.

Would Rob Edwards be a good replacement for John Eustace at Derby County? Tell us in the comments below!

With the international break coming up after Friday's game against Bolton, the Rams should use the time to make a much-needed managerial change, but the jury is out over whether Edwards would be the right man to succeed Eustace.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#2190. Arsenal injury news: Rice, Madueke and Calafiori concerns ahead of Liverpool clash

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal injury news has been in the headlines ahead of their visit to Anfield. Mikel Arteta confirmed Declan Rice, Noni Madueke and Riccardo Calafiori were all sidelined for their Carabao Cup clash against Fleetwood Town on Tuesday.

The Premier League champions lost 5-3 on penalties following their 1-1 draw at Highbury Stadium. Arsenal will face Liverpool at 4.30pm on Sunday. They have a number of injury concerns, plus a suspended teenager to deal with.

When questioned if the three players had just been rested, Arteta replied that Calafiori was unavailable. Madueke had issues with his ankle and Rice was “feeling something on the previous day”, making visible the reason why he has been substituted.

Martin Zubimendi replaced Rice in Saturday’s game when he substituted the player in the 80th minute of the game versus Everton due to Rice grabbing his hamstring. Madueke played till the end of the game. However, he was not spotted in training Monday, and Arteta did not provide any estimation for his return.

Calafiori appears to be in a better place. After being described as having a ‘slight issue’ by Arteta following the Everton game. DaveOCKOP reports that the defender is expected to be available against Anfield.

Winger Christos Tzolis has also been ruled out for five games with a hamstring injury. We’re likely to get an update on how all three are feeling going into the game from Arteta’s pre-match press conference.

Bukayo Saka is still sidelined with a quadriceps injury picked up against Bayern Munich in the Champions League. Arteta said the injury will take “weeks” to recover from, as he needs another scan due to fluid around the area. William Saliba has not played this season due to a back issue and is unlikely to return until December.

Arsenal’s problems were deepened at Highbury. Aaron Loupalo-Bi put Fleetwood ahead in the 21st minute. Viktor Gyokeres equalised five minutes after the restart, shortly after captain Martin Odegaard came on at half-time. Max Dowman was then sent off in the 85th minute for kicking out at Fleetwood’s Harrison Neal.

The 16-year-old will serve a three-match ban, reportedly covering the trip to Liverpool, the home game against Hull and the visit to Newcastle.

Fleetwood scored all five penalties. Odegaard, Kai Havertz and Gyokeres converted for Arsenal. Goalkeeper Jay Lynch saved Bruno Guimaraes’ effort, and 19-year-old defender Conor Haughey scored the winner. It was reportedly the first time the reigning top-flight champions have lost a League Cup tie to a fourth-tier side. There’s 84 places separating the clubs.

Arteta said the result was not down to attitude. “I’m sad, we’re all sad,” he said.

#2189. Willian admits Chelsea exit was a ‘big mistake’ after wanting Arsenal escape just THREE months later

Graduate Sports Journalist with a love for football.

Willian has described leaving Chelsea for Arsenal as a mistake, explaining how quickly his enthusiasm for the move turned into regret.

Speaking to former team-mate John Obi Mikel on The Obi One Podcast, the Brazilian revisited the decision that ended his seven-year Stamford Bridge spell in 2020.

Chelsea offered two more years, while Willian wanted three. His contract-length disagreement with Chelsea featured in ReadChelsea’s coverage at the time.

Arsenal offered the longer deal. Willian also valued keeping his family in London and says Mikel Arteta outlined a central role for him.

“To be honest I should have stayed,” he said, in comments reported by the Mirror.

The winger followed the same route as Petr Cech, who explained his own Chelsea-to-Arsenal move through the desire for regular football.

Willian says the reality differed from the picture presented during talks. Within three months, he had told his agent he wanted to leave.

He linked that frustration to his performances, explaining that unhappiness prevented him from producing his best football.

His Arsenal spell ultimately lasted one season. He scored once in 37 appearances before leaving for Corinthians in 2021.

#2188. Como vs Man Utd Preview: Team news, injuries, form and where to watch

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United travel to Italy on Wednesday, looking for their first win since September 10, when they face Como in the Champions League.

Michael Carrick’s side have struggled to build any momentum this season. Sunday’s 1-1 draw against Leeds extended their winless run to six matches in all competitions, leaving United with just seven points from their opening seven Premier League games.

The pressure on Carrick continues to grow. A win in Europe would offer some relief, but Como will not make life easy for Manchester United.

Manchester United began their Champions League campaign with a convincing 4-0 win over Sabah FK but lost 2-0 to Atletico Madrid in their next match. They have since drawn with Leeds, having also failed to beat Fulham and Tottenham in the Premier League.

Their last six matches across all competitions have produced three draws and three defeats. Michael Carrick is in pressure of his own and needs a response from his players, particularly with United sitting 13th in the Premier League and 13th in the Champions League standings.

Como have shown more promise. Cesc Fabregas’ side beat RB Leipzig 4-1 in Europe before losing 3-2 to Feyenoord. They returned to winning ways against Fiorentina, claiming a 3-1 victory that moved them up to fifth in Serie A, with 14 points from seven games.

Como have scored 11 goals and conceded eight across their last six matches in all competitions. United have struggled, with their only clean sheet of the season coming against Sabah FK.

United have several confirmed absentees ahead of the trip to Italy. Patrick Dorgu, Manuel Ugarte and Benjamin Sesko are ruled out, while Leny Yoro is suspended for the European fixture after picking a red against Atletico Madrid.

Lisandro Martinez is a major concern after coming off at half-time against Leeds with a thigh problem. Ayden Heaven, Luke Shaw and Kobbie Mainoo are all doubtful for the game.

Como will be without Assane Diao, who is sidelined with a thigh injury. Moise Kean has a shin problem and is a doubt, while Trevoh Chalobah is also a fitness concern with a muscular issue.

The match takes place at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia on Wednesday, October 21, with kick-off at 5:45 pm BST.

UK viewers can watch the Champions League fixture live on TNT Sports 2 and HBO Max.

#2187. Arsenal Women vs Benfica: Alessia Russo Hat-Trick Fires Arsenal Women to 3-0 Champions League Win Over Benfica

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal Women vs Benfica: Arsenal Women continued their unbeaten start to the UEFA Women’s Champions League league phase with a convincing 3-0 victory over Benfica at Mangata Developments Stadium on Wednesday night.

Alessia Russo hit a hat trick to claim the spoils and become the top scorer in English Women’s Champions League history. The England international opened the scoring before the break and added two more after the interval.

Despite controlling much of the game Arsenal’s attacking play was stymied by the determined Benfica defence and the inspired Lena Pauels in goal. The German made some stunning saves before Russo finally found a way through.

Arsenal came out firing after their win in the North London derby. Olivia Smith put Pauels under pressure after just 65 seconds.

She made another save soon after as the hosts took control of the game and created a number of great chances.

Geraldine Reuteler made her first start for Arsenal and nearly picked out Smith with a dangerous delivery into the penalty area. Russo also saw an effort blocked following a well-worked set piece.

Georgia Stanway came closest to breaking the deadlock during the opening half-hour. The midfielder escaped her marker before sending a powerful shot towards the bottom corner, but Pauels reacted well to keep the score level.

The Benfica goalkeeper continued her impressive performance by denying Caitlin Foord from the resulting corner.

Benfica gradually grew into the contest and threatened through Froya Dorsin, who wasted an opportunity by firing over the crossbar. The visitors created further pressure before Arsenal regained control.

Russo sent an effort narrowly wide before Smith forced another save from Pauels.

However, Arsenal finally broke through five minutes before half-time. Foord supplied a clever pass into Russo, who placed a precise finish against the far post and into the net.

Arsenal kept their forward momentum going into the second half and nearly extended their lead.

Kyra Cooney-Cross found an excellent ball over the top for Foord but was thwarted by a vital challenge from Catarina Amado.

Foord continued to pose a threat and got on the end of a cross from Ona Batlle at the back post. She powered a header across the goal, but Benfica cleared it in time to stop Russo getting on the end of it.

Smith then tested Pauels again with a deflected effort, but the goalkeeper could not prevent Arsenal from scoring their second.

Russo rose to meet Steph Catley’s corner and headed home to extend the hosts’ lead. The goal was her 22nd in the competition, making her the leading English goalscorer in UEFA Women’s Champions League history.

Benfica responded with a dangerous effort from Andreia Norton, forcing Misa Rodriguez into a good save at her near post.

Arsenal quickly threatened on the counter-attack, with Reuteler rounding Pauels before Diana Gomes cleared her effort off the line.

Pauels kept the game alive for Benfica but made a fantastic save to keep out Smith’s powerful strike in the 15th minute.

But Arsenal finally won the game after Amado brought down Foord inside the penalty box.

Russo stepped up and confidently converted from 12 yards to complete her hat-trick and take her Champions League tally to 23 goals.

Foord thought she had added a fourth during stoppage time, but the officials ruled out her effort for offside.

The result means Arsenal remain undefeated in the league phase of the tournament and also highlights the importance of Russo to the club’s European campaign.

They return to Women’s Super League action on Sunday, November 1, when they play Aston Villa at Emirates Stadium before facing Liverpool. On November 12 they head to Spain to face defending European champions Barcelona.
