#2102. Cristiano Ronaldo announces Portugal retirement after record-breaking 23-year career

Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his retirement from international football.

The 41-year-old made his debut for Portugal in 2003 and has gone on to play 234 times for the national team, scoring 146 goals – both of which are records in the men’s game.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Cristiano Ronaldo (@cristiano)

A post shared by Cristiano Ronaldo (@cristiano)

In a video on social media, Ronaldo said: “To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt of our national team.

“I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the honour and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world.

“Today the time has come to pass it on to the future. It was not an easy decision because some decisions are not made with the mind alone. They are also made with the heart.

“A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end.”

Ronaldo’s announcement comes less than a month after he was suspended for 30 days and fined 255 euros (approximately £210) by the Portuguese Football Federation after walking out on the national team.

The veteran forward left the camp shortly before a Nations League game against Denmark following a row with head coach Jorge Jesus.

He did not reference the incident in his farewell video but admitted he had made “mistakes”.

Ronaldo continued: “When I look back at everything I experienced with the national team, I don’t just see matches, goals records or trophies, I see people.

“I see Portuguese people living abroad who, for 90 minutes, felt a little closer to home. I see millions of Portuguese people I have never met but who became part of my life.

From St Andrews to AI: What happens when underlying business assumptions change?

This can't go on at Celtic – or can it? O'Neill fears and the McGregor dilemma

Scotland set to win tug of war for exciting rising star as rival nation to miss out

“Because, at the end of the day, football is so much bigger than a game. Football is about people.

“Throughout my entire career with the national team, I always pushed myself beyond my limits. I wanted to win. I wanted to be better. I wanted to make history. I always demanded the most of myself. I always wanted more.

“I always believed we could go further. And I gave everything I had for this shirt. There were perfect afternoons and nights, there were victories I will never forget. There were defeats that still hurt to remember.

“I made mistakes. I suffered. There were also moments where I couldn’t give the Portuguese people what they so desperately wanted. But I never gave up and, above all, I never stopped feeling proud to represent Portugal.”

Ronaldo led Portugal to European Championship victory in 2016 as well as winning the Nations League in 2019 and 2025 but World Cup success eluded him.

“Over the years I learned a few very simple things: goals fade, trophies end up in museums, records are eventually broken, but there is something time can never erase, the place we hold in people’s hearts,” continued Ronaldo.

“If I ever made you happy, if one of my goals ever made you embrace someone, forget a worry or feel proud of our country, then it was all worth it.

“Thank you for allowing me to live a dream that began when I was just a little boy in Madeira running after a football.

“The number seven shirt will remain. The pride of having worn it will be mine forever. Portugal will always be a part of me. Farewell, until we meet again.”

#2101. Tottenham new boys score in shoot-out win over Sydney FC

Tottenham Hotspur fans enjoyed their first glimpse of summer signings Andy Robertson and Sandro Tonali in the shirt, with both players scoring penalties in the shoot-out that followed a 1-1 draw with Sydney FC.

Spurs took the lead through a first-half Mathys Tel free-kick, before Roberto De Zerbi’s youthful defence was undone by Takahiro Sekine, who tucked away one of the Australian side’s only chances of the game.

Magic from Mathys Tel 🪄A brilliant free kick from the Frenchman gets @spursofficial off to a flyer, as the striker puts it top bins to take a 1-0 lead in SydneyWatch #TOTvSYD live and exclusive on Paramount+ 📺 pic.twitter.com/ntqTgleasJ

Tonali was brought on as a half-time substitute, before Robertson took the captain’s armband from Archie Gray after he was introduced in the 65th minute.

The former Liverpool left-back delivered three dangerous crosses which went unconverted, something of a theme for a Spurs team who failed to make the most of long spells of dominance.

James Maddison and Mateus Fernandes were not in the match-day squad, while Pedro Porro, Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven and Jean Paul van Hecke have yet to join the group after the World Cup.

There was another impressive showing from 17-year-old prospect Luca Williams-Barnett, who is pushing for first-team opportunities this upcoming season.

Penalties followed the final whistle, with Spurs scoring all four of their spot kicks. Goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, signed on a free transfer this summer, saved one and Sydney FC’s Josh Lacey hit the post to give Spurs the spoils 4-2.

Spurs win the shoot-out 4-2. That will be that.

Hoefsloot dives to his right and pushes Donley’s penalty around the post.

But then Dubravka saves from Popovic, and Spurs remain 3-2 up. Score the next one and they win the shoot-out.

Very similar placing to Tonali’s penalty. Does Dubravka have a save in him?

He doesn’t need to have one because Josh Lacey has hit the post. 3-2 to Spurs after three pens each.

Plenty of power and right into the side netting. No mistake from Spurs’s big money summer signing.

Dubravka then guesses the right way, but Toure finds the bottom left corner. 2-2.

The 17-year-old takes the mickey a little bit, dinking the ball straight down the middle. Spurs score their first penalty.

Then Popovic steps up and sends Dubravka the wrong way. 1-1.

Spurs were the game’s dominant force, but they did not convert that control into enough goals. No cause for alarm though, and no injuries from what we can tell. There will be some penalties on the way.

Williams-Barnett with a superb piece of control and turn forward, but the danger was snuffed out as he dribbled the ball into the penalty area. Then the youngster shoots from outside the box, deflected behind for a corner.

Andy Robertson has been impressive, and the goalkeeper makes a fingertip save to flick his low cross away from danger. Almost third time lucky for Yang who was waiting at the back post for a tap-in.

Andy Robertson's first outing as a Spurs player 🫡 pic.twitter.com/q5bdzQknJ2

Spurs controlling possession, pushing for the goal that would spare them having to take some penalties. As happens with this friendlies, the game has become more bitty since all the changes.

If the game finishes as a draw, there will be a penalty shoot-out. Donley has fizzed some crisp forward passes since coming on in midfield. Then Donley underlaps, picked out by Williams-Barnett but his low cross is straight at the goalkeeper.

Andy Robertson getting forward to good effect once again, standing up a cross for Yang in the middle but the substitute heads wide from seven or eight yards out.

Referee waves play on as Spurs pour forward and Robertson flashes a ball across the box, and the slight deflection was enough to put off Yang at the back post and he missed the target. Should have been a tap in.

Spurs close to a second, but Tonali’s shot from the edge of the box is pushed around the post. There was more good approach play from Williams-Barnett to tee up the Italian.

More Spurs changes: Andy Robertson is on, and takes the armband, he replaces Kyerematen. Up front, Richarlison and Solomon are off, replaced by Min-Hyeok and Dane Scarlett. Donley and Melia replace Gray and Gallagher in midfield.

A couple of appeals for a Spurs penalty after Kyerematen burst beyond the Sydney defence from left-back. He could have crossed sooner, but was tackled, and then there was a challenge on Richarlison. Referee waves it away.

Very youthful Spurs back four on the pitch now, which played a part in the nature of the equaliser they conceded. No Romero, Van de Ven, Van Hecke or Senesi available for selection today, but Andy Robertson is warming up on the touchline.

Spurs straight back into another long spell of possession, with Tonali winning a foul in midfield after a smooth turn forward.

A touch of ill fortunate for Spurs, the half-time substitute Takai inadvertently poked the ball through to Sekine who lifted the ball over Dubravka to equalise. Delicate finish, and Spurs are breached.

Conor Gallagher still closing down tirelessly, but he has been a little untidy with the ball at his feet. I suspect he was the bleep test winner in training. Sydney do well to play through the pressure and keep possession for a while.

Good industry from Tonali in midfield to regain possession, and Williams-Barnett shows real poise on the ball again. Easy to see why Spurs are excited about him.

Kyerematen defends well at the back post when it looked like Macallister was about to head at goal.

Then Spurs are away on the break, and Williams-Barnett skims the crossbar with a left-footed shot from a tight angle.

Three half-time Spurs changes: Tel, Bergvall and Davies off, Takai, Tonali and Williams-Barnett are on. Takai goes to centre-back with 17-year-old Williams-Barnett in an attacking midfield position.

A decent half’s work from Spurs, they look in a good place physically and their high pressing has caught the eye. Not quite clinical enough in the penalty area so far though, they have butchered some good chances.

Sydney have come to life as an attacking force, Spurs’s defence undone by a ball over the top. Dubravka caught in no-man’s-land, and Mac Allister poked the ball beyond him but did not generate enough power to score.

Cracking effort from the Sydney forward Macallister, trying to chip Dubravka from some 45 yards out. The goalkeeper was worried and scrambling, the effort misses the target.

Sydney looking ragged now, and Gallagher cracks a shot off the foot of the post from the edge of the box. Then Youlley takes on a shot from long range which is high, wide and handsome. Richarlison is then fouled by Popovic, dragging down the forward to stop a counter. Yellow card.

Conor Gallagher is charging forward at every opportunity, applying pressure on Sydney’s defenders whenever they have the ball. With no European football, Spurs can really lean into a high-octane approach this season.

Great take, right footed to the the goalkeeper’s side, and the strike was too powerful for Hoefsloot. A clean hit, and Spurs now lead. A well-deserved goal on the balance of play.

The game has slipped into a lull now, after a bright Spurs start. De Zerbi’s team do now have a free-kick at the edge of the D after Manor Solomon is fouled.

Tel amnd Gallagher threaten down the left for Spurs, with the midfielder finding the winger with a reverse pass. Tel’s cross is cleared.

Then Sydney muster their first shot of the game, Youlley with a strike from 25 yards out which Dubravka pushes away from danger.

Sydney FC starting to get their foot on the ball a little more now, but still no sign that they have capability to hurts Spurs going forward. Kyerematen is then fouled in the Sydney half.

Sydney are yet to have a touch in the Spurs penalty area, it has been one-way traffic so far. De Zerbi will be pleased with what he has watched so far, but no killer touch in the box as yet.

Conor Gallagher with a nice touch to win a free-kick near the left touchline. Sydney just about hanging on. The goalkeeper claims Tel’s cross from the free-kick.

Spurs’s closing down is choking Sydney’s build up play, and Gallagher wastes a good chance when free in the box. Shot blocked when there was time and space to pick his spot.

Lucas Bervall’s low cross is turned behind for a corner and Spurs remain in the ascendancy. Another threatening delivery, and Ben Davies may well have had a shout for a penalty, dragged to the turf by Grant. If this was a Premier League game, I’m sure VAR would have taken a close look at that.

Hoefsloot with a really poor pass from his six-yard box, straight into the path of Tel 25 yards out, but his side-footed effort was saved by the goalkeeper. Pitches like this make technical errors an inevitability.

Sydney’s goalkeeper Hoefsloot punches a corner clear under some pressure, attacking set-pieces were a rare positive for Spurs last season. The Premier League team are dominating possession in the early minutes.

Conor Gallagher and Richarlison leading an aggressive Tottenham press in the early exchanges. Tel enjoys plenty of touches down the left flank, but his inswinging cross from the left is headed clear. Rio Kyerematen is puhsing on from left-back.

After a rendition of Oh When The Saints Go Marching In on the trumpet, we are under way. A chance for Aussie Spurs fans to feel like they are in N17 for the evening.

The pitch looks slightly more lush than the surface Chelsea had to play on across town yesterday. The Allianz Stadium looks distinctly similar to the Etihad. Archie Gray captains Spurs.

No James Maddison in the squad for this game, perhaps still being managed physically after last year’s serious knee injury. Suspect we will see a more senior side picked for the friendly against Chelsea on Saturday.

The 21-year-old has a sweet left foot, on display when he scored this goal against Manchester City while on loan at Leyton Orient.

JAMIE DONLEY. THAT'S INCREDIBLE. 🤯The @SpursOfficial loanee with an incredible effort from distance that ends up in the net to give @leytonorientfc the opening goal against Manchester City 😱#EmiratesFACup pic.twitter.com/bHnKg92Q2y

Lucas Bergvall has been linked with a move away from Spurs, but he starts in midfield. No Fernandes in the squad at all. No summer signings in the starting line-up, but Tonali and Andy Robertson are on the bench.

Spurs starting XI: Dubravka; Kyerematen, Davies, Hardy, Tye Hall; Gray, Bergvall, Solomon, Gallagher, Tel; Richarlison

Subs: Kinsky, Robertson, Takai, Tingey, Byrne, Tyrese Hall, Russell-Denny, Donley, Tonali, Ajayi, Yang, Williams-Barnett, Scarlett

Spurs fans took their first look at summer signing Mateus Fernandes in a 2-0 victory over Auckland, and their pre-season tour continues today against Sydney FC.

Fernandes, an £85m purchase from West Ham United, also scored a stunning volley in a behind-closed-doors game against MK Dons.

Sandro Tonali is part of the travelling squad for these friendlies, as is new centre-back Jean Paul van Hecke. Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero and Pedro Porro have been given extra time off after their respective nations reached the World Cup final, won by Porro and Spain.

Van Hecke and Senesi ranked very highly among defenders for progressive passing, which offers an insight into the qualities Roberto De Zerbi is prioritising this summer.

The Italian likes his teams to bait opponents into pressing them high up the pitch, before moving the ball through central areas using third-man combinations and wall passes. The addition of two ball-playing centre-backs and two new central midfielders should mean Spurs can play like a recognisable De Zerbi team.

While Dane Scarlett and Richarlison scored against Auckland, Spurs’s squad still lacks high-class options in forward areas, with a move for Bournemouth’s Eli Junior Kroupi mooted earlier in the summer.

Spurs fans will be excited to watch 17-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett, the midfielder who is one of the outstanding players in his age group in the country.

“He’s a talent,” Ledley King said. “There’s a lot of hard work ahead of him, but there’s no doubt that he’s someone with great ability.

“He’s seen players like Harry Kane come through the academy and, through sheer hard work and determination, put themselves in a position to kick on. He couldn’t have a better role model.

“There’s no doubt we’re excited by his talent and the next part will be up to him.”

#2100. ‘Hopefully…’ – Andoni Iraola hints at potential Ryan Gravenberch return date after injury blow

Andoni Iraola has provided an update on the injury which has ruled Ryan Gravenberch out of Liverpool’s Champions League fixture against Fenerbahce.

The Merseyside club confirmed on Tuesday morning that the midfielder hasn’t travelled with the rest of the squad for the game in Istanbul tomorrow due to a heel injury and will instead undergo recovery at the AXA Training Centre.

While that obviously comes as a body blow for the Reds for the match against Dirk Kuyt’s side, it appears that the 24-year-old is unlikely to be sidelined for long.

Iraola was prompted for an update on Gravenberch during his pre-match press conference in Istanbul this afternoon, and the Liverpool head coach is hopeful that the Dutchman will be cleared to resume playing quickly.

The Reds boss said (via Liverpool Echo): “It’s a day-to-day thing. It’s a heel injury. He’s had some discomfort. He was warming up against Arsenal and was not 100%. Hopefully he can be available for the weekend, but we cannot say for sure.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

If Iraola has left the door open for Gravenberch to potentially return against Crystal Palace next Sunday, it suggests that the midfielder’s injury is relatively minor.

The 24-year-old mightn’t make it back in time for the visit to Selhurst Park, but the two-week international window should hopefully enable him to be fully fit for the grudge match against Manchester United later this month.

The Dutchman was criticised for his performance against Chelsea in the Carabao Cup last week and in recent games has been disapponting by his standards, but he remains a vital player to Liverpool and one of the best midfielders in the Premier League when operating at his top level.

Even if he’s cleared to play on Sunday, Gravenberch seems unlikely to start given the form of Alexis Mac Allister and Trey Nyoni in the middle of the park, and he mightn’t be able to feature for a full 90 minutes if he’s touch-and-go for the weekend.

Fingers crossed that our number 38 will at least be available to Iraola when the Reds take on Palace with one eye on revenge for their last-gasp defeat in this fixture last season.

#2099. Falkirk 2-0 Celtic: Pressure is mounting on Martin O'Neill as Scottish giants suffer a sixth defeat in 10 matches - as hosts celebrate their first win over Bhoys since 2007

Published: 10:11 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 10:55 EDT, 1 November 2026

Celtic paid the price for a sloppy start and a superb display from former goalkeeper Scott Bain as they fell to a 2-0 defeat at Falkirk.

Ethan Ross netted in the third minute after a mistake by Cameron Carter-Vickers and Scott Tanser put Falkirk two ahead in the 38th minute.

Bain made ten saves as Martin O’Neill’s side endured an afternoon of frustration and suffered a sixth defeat in ten matches.

The champions remain four points clear at the top of the William Hill Premiership but have now played a game more than second-placed Rangers.

Falkirk moved up to fourth in the table after their fourth consecutive victory and their first over Celtic since 2007.

Carter-Vickers returned to the starting line-up after injury, while Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain was handed his first start in two months. Winger Haissem Hassan was recalled.

Kasper Hogh might have fancied himself to end his barren run on Falkirk’s synthetic pitch given most of his career goals have come on artificial surfaces, but the former Bodo/Glimt striker was dropped as Camilo Duran led the line.

Martin O'Neill looks on in dismay as Celtic suffer in Falkirk

The Danish striker came on for the final 25 minutes but was barely involved as he went 14 games without a goal.

#2098. Mikel Arteta's mission to conquer his Anfield demons: Why Arsenal boss must overcome psychological damage from his playing days and take the handbrake off as he plots first win at Liverpool, writes ISAAN KHAN

Published: 08:47 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 11:13 EDT, 1 November 2026

The word 'Anfield' still haunts Mikel Arteta.

It was there, 12 years ago, that the Spaniard suffered a chastening experience after losing 5-1 there as an Arsenal player in February 2014.

In a subsequent interview with Spanish newspaper Marca, Arteta used the term 'pajara' - a Spanish phrase com monly associated with cyclists who suddenly run out of energy - to describe a sensation mirroring mental paralysis. He had been caught up in an Anfield tornado.

'Suddenly I could only see red shirts flying around, the game is passing all over me and I cannot react,' Arteta reflected.

'Everyone is thinking, 'What is he doing?' I cannot react, emotionally, physical. I cannot cope, everything goes fast and I only had that feeling in my career once - and it was at Anfield.'

Such was the impact of that trauma that Arteta felt compelled to bring a slice of Anfield to Arsenal's London Colney base ahead of a league meeting in November 2021.

Mikel Arteta (right) has consistently found life tough when managing away at Anfield

Going to Anfield has become something akin to a hoodoo - and it shows no signs of abating

Arteta surrounded the training pitch with enormous speakers which blared out 'You'll Never Walk Alone' during a training session, in hope the noise would ready his players to tackle the very atmosphere he himself wilted in. It was to no avail.

The Gunners found themselves on the end of a 4-0 drubbing and Arteta on the end of mocking from critics for his alternative methods.

Five years later, Arsenal's away day hoodoo against the Reds has shown no signs of abating.

The north London club's league record against Liverpool away under Arteta reads: six games, three draws, three defeats. Arsenal's most recent league victory there was in September 2012, in which Arteta played in the 2-0 victory.

Their results against Manchester City at the Etihad - their other closest title rivals in recent years - under Arteta are no better either. Seven games have resulted in five defeats and two draws.

In fact, across the 27 Premier League teams Arteta's Arsenal have faced away from home during his seven-year reign, his lowest points-per-game ratios are against Man City (0.29) and Liverpool (0.50).

These matches are more than difficult away trips. They are a test of both Arteta's tactical flexibility and the psycho logical resilience of his team in the face of hostility.

Andoni Iraola's side have appeared to turn a corner in the league after beating the impressive Brighton last weekend. With a cloud of uncertainty hanging over Man City and whether their sanctions for breaching financial rules will be enacted before the season ends, Liverpool may well end up as Arsenal's closest challengers for the title.

Beating Arsenal on Sunday, certainly, would go some way to announcing themselves as true contenders.

Arsenal are champions but they have consistently struggled away against the very best teams

So where have Arteta's Arsenal gone wrong at Anfield and the Etihad Stadium? Well, Arteta's tactical approach has arguably been too cautious in these fixtures for a start.

The 1-0 defeat in August 2025 against Arne Slot's Liverpool smacked of restraint and a concession that a point would be good enough before Dominik Szoboszlai's stunning late free-kick winner.

Arsenal's defensive organisation has long been a major strength under Arteta. He has built his Arsenal from the backline, reinforcing it with excellent back-up options before assessing the forward positions.

Yet, in these high-profile away matches, the pursuit of defensive security can come at the expense of attacking ambition.

There's a big drop in attacking output between when Arsenal face Liverpool at Anfield under Arteta compared with when the Gunners face other league opponents on away turf across the last two seasons.

Possession drops from 56.3 to 43.2 per cent, expected goals from 1.6 to 1.1 and big chances created from 3.1 to 1.8.

The impact of the fervent Anfield atmosphere can't be ignored, either. Ray Parlour understands this better than most, making his Arsenal debut at Anfield in January 1992 aged 18.

The Gunners legend, part of Arsene Wenger's Invincibles side, has a word of advice for the current crop.

'I made my debut there, I know exactly how tough it is to play there. But mentally, you've got to get ready,' Parlour tells Daily Mail Sport.

'For me, the crowd in the first 15 to 20 minutes is always very important at Anfield, because you have to silence them if you can.

Arteta's attack routinely suffers as he seeks defensive solidity in the toughest away games

Arsenal are very strong when they score first but slow starts have proven their Achilles heel

'You've got to start on the front foot, put them under pressure, and I think they can leak goals, Liverpool. To try score that first goal is always important.

'We know defensively Arsenal are a very strong side, so if they go and get that first goal, then they might have a good afternoon there.'

Parlour raises a pertinent point. Arsenal's slow starts at Anfield have left themselves with a mountain to climb. Of the 26 league games Arsenal won last season, they scored first in 24 of those matches. Whereas in the six away matches against Liverpool under Arteta, the Gunners have taken time to getting going.

More shots (from 27 to 30) and an increased xG (from 3.2 to 3.5) were registered in the second period compared to the first half in those games.

Arsenal need to start quicker - and be more clinical, too. At the Emirates, Arteta's men have struck 10 goals against Liverpool, but just six at Anfield despite creating more big chances at Anfield (1.8 per away game vs 1.1 per home game).

Parlour references Arsenal's 3-0 pummelling at Brighton last month as a key example. Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler admitted telling his players to 'win the small battles first' and that's exactly what they did.

'Win the first header, win the first tackle, win the first throw in, win the first corner,' revealed Hurzeler when asked about his pre-match message to his players. The Gunners can use this as a lesson to overcome their bogey team.

'Look, they're champions. They've got to play in all different sort of atmospheres,' explains Parlour.

'There's a lot of experienced players out there, so you know what to expect.

Arteta played in Arsenal's last league win at Anfield - a 2-0 victory 14 years ago against Brendan Rodgers' Liverpool. He will look to end that streak as a manager on Sunday

Former Arsenal midfielder Ray Parlour wants to see a bravery that can help navigate the storm

'It's going to be a tough place to play, but you've just got to go there and play your game. Individuals win their battles, which is very important in football.

'You see Brighton when they turned over Arsenal, they won their battles that day, so you've got to make sure you get one over on the players you're playing against.

Ultimately, if Arteta is to banish the Anfield demons that have lingered for 12 years, Arsenal must arrive with the courage to impose themselves from the first whistle - and the resilience to withstand the inevitable storm. Only then can the Spaniard finally rewrite a story that has haunted him for so long.

#2097. ‘Painful’ – Alexis Mac Allister doesn’t hold back about ‘unpleasant situation’ at Liverpool

Alexis Mac Allister has spoken out about his ‘painful, unpleasant situation’ at Liverpool in terms of not being offered a new contract.

The Argentine caused a stir in September when he said that he was ‘very sad‘ not to have been offered a new deal by the club, having seen fellow 2023 signings Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai both pen contract extensions earlier this year.

The Telegraph’s Dominic King reported last month that Anfield chiefs aren’t in ‘any rush’ to begin talks over a new deal for the Reds’ number 10 (who’s contracted to June 2028), despite his resurgence in form since the start of this season.

Appearing on the Los Edul show in his homeland, Mac Allister spoke candidly about Liverpool’s decision not to offer him new terms over the past few months.

The 27-year-old said: “We’re in a situation where I have a year and a half left on my contract. Last season I was told that the club’s idea was not to renew it, at least for now, and obviously that was a painful, unpleasant situation.”

When asked if the situation was making him despondent, he replied: “Not that much, because at the end of the day, I still had – and still have – time left at this club, which is what I want most – to stay here.

“The reality is that the manager has now changed, the sporting director has changed, and new investors are coming into the club, so I think I’m now in a position where anything can happen. We’ll see what happens in the future. I’ve always said that I’m very happy here, that I really enjoy it, and we’ll see.”

Mac Allister added: “Look at Szoboszlai and Gravenberch. They’re two players who were in the same contractual situation as me, and when I was told that, they renewed their contracts.

“It was more a position taken by the club, and generally that’s how things are done. At the end of the day, as a club you don’t want to lose a lot of money, and you don’t want players leaving on free transfers either.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

That the Argentine has spoken out publicly about his contract situation once more gives a strong hint that privately he’s seething at not being offered a new deal in the same way that Szoboszlai and Gravenberch were.

Admittedly Mac Allister’s collapse in form last season may have triggered a reluctance from the club to commit to a contract extension for a player who’ll be 29 when his current terms expire, and he’s a bit older than his aforementioned midfield teammates.

However, the ex-Brighton man has been excellent in the first two months of this campaign, almost as though he’s motivated by a burning desire to earn a new deal at Anfield and show that the hierarchy have been mistaken in their reluctance to tie him down for the long-term.

The 2022 World Cup winner is currently on £180,000 per week at Liverpool, a figure exceeded by 10 of his teammates (Capology), and it could be the case that he’s seeking a higher amount than what the club are prepared to offer him.

Mac Allister could hardly have made his desire for a new contract any clearer. We don’t know exactly why his situation is taking longer to resolve than those of Szoboszlai and Gravenberch, but if he keeps performing on the pitch, then surely it’s just a matter of when and not if he’s offered an extension by the Anfield hierarchy.

#2095. Mikey Moore trapped in a German nightmare as Rangers loan hero caught in a 'mess'

Mikey Moore’s loan spell at FC Koln has been branded a “mess” by German media with the former Rangers loan star failing to register a goal or assist in his first eight appearances.

Moore - who started Tottenham's Premier League opener before his loan exit - netted seven times and claimed eight assists in 47 outings at Ibrox last season before returning to Spurs and heading to the Bundesliga.

The winger has teamed up in Germany with ex-Celtic defender Jahmai Simpson-Pusey and highly-rated English prospect Reigan Heskey, son of former Liverpool and England striker Emile.

But Moore has been unable to hit the ground running at Koln and was once again forced to settle for a place on the bench for Saturday’s 1-1 draw away to Union Berlin.

Read more: The telling Michael Nicholson quip that reveals Celtic's transfer strategy

The England Under-20 international was introduced as a substitute, but his wait for a first goal contribution in Germany continued. And afterwards, leading German outlet BILD delivered a scathing assessment of his performances so far.

Fellow German outlet Express has gone one step further, claiming Moore is becoming “impatient” over his lack of minutes and suggesting the youngster is simply trying too hard to make things happen when his opportunities arrive.

Koln boss Rene Wagner admits seeing Moore finally break his duck with a goal or assist remains on his “personal bingo card”, although he insists the youngster has already shown enough to suggest he can make a success of his spell in Germany.

Speaking after the draw with Union, Wagner said: “An assist or a goal from Mikey Moore would still be on my personal bingo card.”

Asked about the decision to leave Moore on the bench, he explained: “Mikey started against Schalke and in the cup. He’s already shown from the bench that he can bring a lot of energy. That was the idea. We wanted to become dangerous again late in the game with his substitution.

“We anticipated Union would play with a back five and wanted to have two holding midfielders on the pitch to be able to switch formations effectively. We had to do that after just five minutes.”

#2094. “I’m not Mo Salah” – Bradley Barcola speaks defiantly about his big-money Liverpool transfer

Bradley Barcola has said that he doesn’t feel any pressure to try and emulate Mo Salah at Liverpool and is instead focusing on creating his own legacy at Anfield.

At the end of the summer, the Reds spent an initial £106m (potentially rising to £123m, via The Athletic) to sign the French winger from Paris Saint-Germain, with the 24-year-old effectively brought in as the right-sided replacement for the Egyptian King.

It took the new signing seven matches to get off the mark for LFC, with that famine turning to feast in the form of a hat-trick against LASK in mid-October, and he’s followed that up with assists in the wins over Brentford and Brighton (Transfermarkt).

In an interview with Sky Sports, Barcola defiantly insisted that he doesn’t feel a burden to emulate Salah or repay the substantial transfer fee paid for him, with his sole focus being to make his ‘own mark’ and let his performances do the talking.

The France winger said: “First of all, I wasn’t the one who decided the transfer fee, so that’s not been my problem.

“Regarding Mo Salah, he’s a legend here, a huge one. He’s done big things here and, for that, I have an enormous respect for him, but it’s not pressure for me at all.

“I’m not Mo Salah, so I’m going to try to contribute whatever I can to the club and make my own mark on its history. I don’t feel any pressure about that.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Whoever was signed as the effective replacement for the legendary Egyptian was always going to face inevitable comparisons with our former no.11, but such were the standards set by Salah that striving to emulate him would be near-impossible.

Nobody is expecting Barcola to match the Trabzonspor man’s 257-goal tally for Liverpool over a nine-year period. As the Frenchman acknowledged, his job is simply to deliver the best that he can for the Reds.

There have been some moments to forget in his first few weeks on Merseyside, such as the missed sitter against Brentford last month, but he also conjured up a tremendous assist for Alexander Isak’s winning goal in the same match.

The 24-year-old might’ve drawn a blank against Arsenal on Sunday, but his direct running along the left flank was difficult for the Gunners to contain during the first half in particular, offering the kind of proactive threat that we love to see from wingers playing for LFC.

Salah was a unique figure at Liverpool, and Barcola doesn’t strictly have to emulate what the Egyptian has done in order to be regarded as a success at Anfield in time to come. We’ve seen glimpses of what he can offer to the Reds, and time is very much on his side to build upon that promising start.

#2092. My Rangers 'not going to chuck it' admission as I chase senior milestones

Findlay Curtis insists he is there for the long run at Rangers and Scotland as he looks to cement his place for club and country.

The 20-year-old attacker, who came through the Ibrox academy, had a successful loan spell at Kilmarnock last season and returned to the Light Blues looking to kick on.

However, he has made most of his recent appearances off the bench as Derek McInnes’s side have gone on a 11-game unbeaten run which has taken them into second place in the William Hill Premiership ahead of the trip to St Mirren on Saturday and secured a place in the Premier Sports Cup final against Hibernian next month.

Despite a lack of recent starts Curtis was named in Sebastien Pocognoli’s first Scotland squad for the Nations League camp in September and October and then dropped to the Under-21s where he starred in the 5–2 victory over Azerbaijan Under-21s at Rugby Park.

Curtis returned to the senior squad and came off the bench in the 2-1 home defeat to Slovenia and on Tuesday it was revealed that he had retained his place in the squad for this month’s final two Group B1 matches against North Macedonia and Switzerland.

The Gers youngster is ready to do whatever it takes to become a regular for the Light Blues and in dark blue.

He said: “He (Pocognoli) just wanted me to be myself. You saw it in the last camp. I was in for the first couple of days and then I dropped down to the Under-21s. I knew I wasn’t going to get enough game time, so I think I had to go and prove myself a bit.

Derek McInnes makes Rangers transfer stance crystal clear over in-form star

Rangers injury latest as key duo target Hampden return and two near comeback

“It’s every young boy’s dream. I’m just delighted to be back up for this camp and hopefully I can make that impact again.

“I think if you have to drop down a level, all you can do is be the best you can be. I think I did that. I’m not going to chuck it at any time, whether it’s at club level, with Scotland or with Scotland Under-21s.

“But all the boys have been brilliant so far and hopefully we can have success this year.”

#2091. O'Neill admits new signings are struggling with demands of being a Celtic player after dispiriting loss at Falkirk

Published: 11:08 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 11:21 EDT, 1 November 2026

Celtic boss Martin O’Neill admitted his summer recruits need to prove that they have the character and quality to handle the pressure of playing for the club.

The league leaders went down 2-0 at Falkirk on Sunday afternoon – their sixth defeat in their last 10 in all competitions – as they missed the chance to extend their advantage at the top of the Premiership table to seven points.

First-half strikes from Ethan Ross and Scott Tanser had the Bairns ahead at the break, and despite peppering Scott Bain’s goal in the second period, the visitors were unable to find a response.

When it was put to O’Neill that some new members of his squad are still struggling to meet the club’s high expectations, he said: ‘Absolutely. You have to cope with the pressure to be a player.

‘Tommy Burns said it might be easier to play against Celtic than for Celtic but hopefully we have enough in the dressing room and players who have been big winners.

‘When you ask managers sometimes you think the best team is the one that has won convincingly, but there are a number of players who have arrived.

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill was unhappy with his team's defending at Falkirk

‘You can think someone is doing well in training but the only place to find where players fit is out there.

‘We’re not used to losing a lot of games. We were in a much worse position this time last year so we have to buckle down and win a game and win a game in Europe. Thursday [against Besiktas in the Europa League] is a big game and then the following Sunday is massive before we go into the international break.

‘We need to sort out a few things. I was asked about confidence. If you take Kasper [Hogh], he wanted to get a goal after some time.

‘Something might fall for him but it’s not just that something might fall for you. You have to work at it which is something us as a team and the players in particular need to do.’

O’Neill bemoaned the defensive lapses that allowed Falkirk to open up a two-goal cushion, but saw enough in his team’s performance in the attacking third to give him confidence that things will soon start clicking.

‘I’m naturally disappointed to have lost the game,’ he said. ‘We had a lot of chances. Their goalie was magnificent but naturally we’ve lost so I’m very disappointed.

Callum McGregor looks frustrated as Celtic are made to suffer in Falkirk

‘The goals were very poor from our viewpoint. We didn’t clear it for the first one then we let someone run through and pick his spot for the second. We had some really great chances we just weren’t able to convert.

‘At half-time I thought we were still in the game. I thought we’d played decent stuff. If you concede a magnificent goal you take it in your stride.

‘When you concede a bad goal, which from any viewpoint was a poor goal, then it’s tough to come back then the goalie makes some saves and it’s frustrating.

‘Despite mistakes at the back we had enough chances to get back.

‘We have conceded some poor goals and haven’t kept a clean sheet for some time which is the essence of a championship team, but we’re still top and we need to address it and that’s the way out of it.

‘We scored seven against Hearts which isn’t that long ago. I just thought the goalie had a magnificent game and we should have scored a number in each half.

‘When you don’t it becomes frustrating. We have to address that we were conceding. Hopefully we can still do that. It’s still a long season.’

Bust a gut to cover and thwart Hibs’ explosive breaks. Produced a number of excellent blocks, most notably one that denied Elding.

Stood up well when Hearts needed him. His outstanding sliding block to thwart Passlack late in the game was as good as a goal.

Left the field after just 14 minutes with a horrible head knock, picked up when he nodded Calvin Miller’s cross narrowly wide.

Outnumbered in the first half, he looked lost in midfield. Far more influential when Hearts later got a grip of that department.

Stretched his opponents as Hearts grew into the game, but never really came up with a telling pass or effort on goal.

Caused all sorts of problems with his early crosses, only to become the latest addition to Hearts’ ridiculous injury list. Hobbled off before the interval.

Quiet in the first half, save for a perfect cross that Braga should have converted. Direct, dangerous and back to his best after the interval.

Claudio Braga misses a late chance to force extra time in the Premier Sports Cup semi-final

#2087. City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier  League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

Lavelli blasts his shot down the middle, and Inter have won the Asahi Trophy!

The teenager sizes things up, and sends Donnarumma the other way.

A stuttering run, and Provedel beats it away.

Frattesi misses! Donnarumma stretches out and flings up his left arm for a great save.

Khusanov misses, firmly striking against the post.

Donnarumma dives to the right, the shot in the opposite direction.

Rayan Ait-Nouri misses! Spooned over the bar.

We’re onto the penalty shootout. The pressure builds for the Asahi Trophy.

Echeverri is fouled in midfield, he takes it quickly, but the move breaks down and Inter get back into position again. The end nears.

Three more minutes of this have been indicated.

Gonzalez finds McAidoo, and City look for room on the right. Inter sit back and stay compact.

The game has slowed to a near-halt. It seems everyone is resigned to penalties.

Ait-Nouri finds McAidoo’s run to the back post with a fabulous low cross, but the winger’s return ball is cut out by Provedel.

If McAidoo does not stay on at City for the season ahead, you’d expect plenty of sides to be looking to bring him in on loan.

Ait-Nouri is offside as he takes the ball on the left wing, and Inter have it back briefly.

McAidoo yet again gets forward and almost forces a cross past Provedel. The ball comes back to Sangare, but his effort is blocked. City are getting closer.

Khusanov is booked for a foul in midfield, and then is on hand to block a shot on the line as Inter fail to convert.

McAidoo, yet again. A shot to the far post, yet again. A miss, yet again. He looks dangerous though.

McAidoo repeats the trick, but this time he keeps his shot low and hits the bottom of the far post. The best moment of the half so far.

However, with the scores still level, it’s only 10 minutes from a penalty shootout.

McAidoo scoots into the box from the right and curls a shot wide of the far post.

Enzo makes another change 🔄 pic.twitter.com/afvwMFYlB9

Savinho slices a shot wildly high and wide. Changes are coming.

Reis claims to meet a corner at the back post, but it comes off an Inter player. The corner switches to the right, and this one is cleared, for now. City keep the ball and Ait-Nouri picks out Gonzalez’s run, and he strains to shin it over.

Lewis has the ball in the box after quick feet from Savinho with the assist, and he prods the ball at Provedel.

Foden and Semenyo off, Sangare and Echeverri on. Lewis is City’s new captain.

On the front foot 👊 pic.twitter.com/AZC7UXYXrj

Foden sends in a corner, and Reis hooks a volley against the bar as the ball drops. Gonzalez gets back up to his feet slowly after that phase of play, and then sits back down as he awaits treatment.

City are camped in Inter’s half now, which is an improvement on the last half where it was more even, territorially.

McAidoo is released down the inside left, he clears his marker and aims for Semenyo, but Bisseck clears for a corner.

Pavard goes down after he is caught late from Ait-Nouri, but he’s fine to continue.

More subs now  Topalovic replaces Stankovic. Provedel replaces Martinez in goal.

Savinho might be the most dangerous player for City today, a sentence that has rarely been true in the last couple of years. McAidoo whips in a cross, which Henrique clears under no pressure.

Reis and Alleyne are the central defenders. Ait-Nouri is on the left, and Khusanov the right.

Stankovic gets a yellow as Savinho sprints down the inside left away from Inter Milan players. McAidoo is then tripped by Augusto, who hurt himself doing so.

A decent enough corner from Foden who swings the ball close to the back post, but the goalkeeper Martinez is fouled as the ball comes in.

The full slate of City changes, as Lewis has a shot blocked when a corner is not properly cleared. Savinho stands a cross up, but it comes to nothing. Khusanov has a shot scrambled away.

Enzo makes 5️⃣ changes at the beginning of the second half 🔄Watch LIVE on CITY+ https://t.co/rVv0RHMeAC pic.twitter.com/TIrLvBlkN3

Reis and Mcaidoo, Ait-Nouri, Alleyne, and Gonzalez are on for City, with Gviardiol one of the players going off, as is Reijnders.

Frattesi, Henrique, Mosconi, Zielinski and Bastoni are the five Inter introductions, but there are more. Mkhitrayan has gone off, with Diouf, Idrrissou, and Augusto some of the exits too.

We go again. A billion subs have been made. So far, Frattesi is on. Let’s see what we know about the rest. Ait-Nouri is on.

It’s been more or less what you expect from a pre-season friendly in the humidity.

The players are yet to shake off their summer ice creams and really get sharp again, but there are some flashes of ability here and there.

Reijnders releases Semenyo, the Dutchman plays the ball into Savinho, who dances to the byline, pulls it back, but it’s then cleared from Bisseck.

That’s it for the half, and the action restarts in 15 minutes.

Savinho wriggles into the box but just fails to find Semenyo.

Mkhitaryan concedes a foul on Lewis in midfeild, and the half appears to be drifting to a bloodless close.

Savinho, maybe in his last game for City, brings the ball high up the right but then City are forced all the way back to Donnarumma.

City are not panicked by keeping the ball, and they look for a fresh opening.

Foden commits his own foul in midfield, this time on Mkhitaryan. There are a few minutes left before half-time, at which point we may see a few changes from both sides given the early stage of pre-season.

Foden swings in a corner that Savinho briefly keeps alive before Diouf clears, and Dimarco cannot quite reach the ball before it’s played back to Donnarumma.

Barella fouls Reijnders in midfield, but it’s nothing vicious.

Semenyo clips in a dangerous-looking cross from the left wing, but it’s deflected behind for a corner on the right.

Foden is tugged down in midfield, with the City man still failing to show much of his talent in the new season.

Mkhitaryan continues to find space in pockets on the left. In general, Inter are finding it very easy to trundle to the edge of the City box.

Donnarumma flaps at a cross, and Savinho and Lewis work to clear it momentarily.

Do you think the players are coping without a hydration break?

Dimarco is fed by Diouf, with the right wing-back finding the left wing-back. He’s on the right side of the pitch too, oddly, but his left-footed shot is far from dreadful, but easily stopped by Donnarumma.

City have some pressure and Kovacic hits a group of defenders with a volley from outside the box. It’s meek stuff from Maresca’s men so far but obviously, too early to draw much from it.

City are looking to build from the back through the middle, but they are quickly crowded out. Inter come forward once more.

Diouf forces a corner on the right wing as Donnarumma clears a cross. It’s taken short, Inter switch the ball left, but Mkhitaryan overhits a pass to the byline.

Mkhitaryan receives the ball on the left, inside the box, in another dangerous position. Lewis had drifted  too far inside, but the danger passes when the forward is flagged offside.

Inter are keeping the ball calmly at the back, finding spaces between the pressing City attackers.

They break through and Donnarumma beats away a low shot from Stankovic.

Benjmain Pavard scores! Manchester City fail to clear their lines and Pavard, who started the move, is on hope to finish with the keeper stricken.

Divin Mubamba gets the opener! Semenyo beats his right-bacck and crosses to the six-yard box for Mubamba to tap in.

14. Wonderful work from Semenyo 👊He beats his man on the left to get to the byline, squares it across goal and Divin converts from close range 🎯🐝 1-0 ⚪️ https://t.co/pCDrkfriLY

Dimarco volleys wide but he too was offside, and then Martinez saves from Reijnders at the other end. It’s a free-flowing match so far.

Stankovic goes close with an early header after Inter win their first corner of the match. It’s an open game so far.

City win two early corners, but they are both cleared. A bright start for the Premier League side. Esposito then goes close at the other end, but he was offside anyway.

A recent on-pitch spat over the captain’s armband between Liverpool players demonstrated that these friendlies are not simply warm-ups.

If there are problems at the club, you can pick up on them here.

The fans are out in force in Hong Kong, where the Premier League continues to dominate attention.

Here’s what the former striker told Manchester City: “I’m looking forward to it. I’m not sure Enzo is going to change that much but some tweaks here and there.

“People talking about it being similar to when [Alex] Ferguson left but I don’t think it’s the same, they didn’t have the same infrastructure. He’s a top manager. He will want to put his own stamp on it.”

The biggest story in football right now is increasingly hard to ignore.

Gianni Infantino’s ludicrous plan was sunk almost as soon as it was announced, then he defended himself with such verve as to make himself look completely isolated and apart from the organisation itself, and now UEFA has said it is calling time.

The governing body says it has lost faith in the Peace Prize inventor, a problem which had been in the post for a while now.

The two London sides are facing off in their own pre-season friendly.

You can follow that live here, and find out which player has been sent off.

In their little costumes ahead of kick-off.

The venue in Hong Kong is decent enough and has started filling out. It’s a jaunty 26 degrees, 92% humidity, and raining too. It’s just like being in London during your worst nightmares, basically.

We’ll see how this continues, and if it does continue, over the coming weeks, but Phil Foden has the nod as captain for Enzo Maresca tonight.

Foden signed a new contract recently but has been well off his consistent best for some time now. Another poor season would put him in the frame for the exit door next summer, so this is a chance.

Captaining the side in Enzo's first match as boss 👍©️ pic.twitter.com/bcvIhwXMas

Here is an examination on how Manchester City’s early, £116 million deal left the rest of the transfer market dealing with the implications.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester City and Inter Milan.

The two sides meet  at Kai Tak Sports Park, Hong  Kong as their pre-season work kicks up a gear ahead of the new campaign.

City are still getting used to life without Pep Guardiola, the coach who left after a decade of high spending and high performance.

In his place is Enzo Maresca, who is not shy with the chequebook himself.

Ayyoub Bouaddi, the outstanding 18-year-old Moroccan international, should soon arrive from Lille when a fee is agreed, but Elliot Anderson and Jeremy Monga have already been signed.

City were runners-up last season, so Maresca is under pressure not just to keep things going without Guardiola, but to get the team back to the top of English football. That looks to be a tough prospect with Arsenal likely to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle in the coming days.

Inter, meanwhile, have swooped to pick up John Stones on a free transfer after his contract ended at the Etihad Stadium, and he is joined by Manuel Akanji, another former City centre-back whose loan turned permanent in the summer.

Inter won Serie A last season under head coach Cristian Chivu, and they are still one of the best sides in Europe.

While this friendly is likely to be played at a reduced pace, and will be disrupted by rustiness and substitutes, we could still learn a lot about both sides going into the new campaign, and there may be the odd surprise thrown up by a young player looking to stake a claim ahead of his senior colleagues this year.

#2086. ‘Big call’ – Journalists react as Iraola names ‘exciting line-up’ for Liverpool in Istanbul

Andoni Iraola has made five changes to the Liverpool starting XI for tonight’s Champions League clash against Fenerbahce, with the head coach not afraid to drop some big names to the substitutes’ bench.

There’s a signficant reshuffle in attack as Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Alexander Isak are all taken out of the line-up, with Dominik Szoboszlai, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz coming in to start.

The Reds have no recognised centre-forward in their starting XI, so it looks likely that Bradley Barcola will move infield to lead the line.

When the team news was announced 75 minutes before kick-off, two Liverpool Echo reporters covering the game in Istanbul gave their immediate takes to some eye-catching selections by Iraola.

Paul Gorst wrote on the live matchday blog: ‘No recognised striker for Liverpool, so my hunch is it is Bradley Barcola who will lead the line tonight. It’s an exciting line-up, though. Munoz, Ngumoha, Szoboszlai all in there alongside Barcola.’

Ian Doyle focused on Trey Nyoni keeping his place alongside Alexis Mac Allister, saying: ‘Nyoni starts a third successive game, which is a big call. Not on form, but in terms of fitness for a youngster.’

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

A relentless fixture list and a quick turnaround from the defeat to Arsenal on Sunday has no doubt been a factor in Iraola making so many changes, but it’s by no means a weak starting XI for Liverpool.

The full-back combination of Joe Gomez and Kostas Tsimikas may seem surprising, but both are experienced campaigners who won’t wilt in the intense atmosphere of the Sukru Saracoglu Stadium.

The decision to persist with Nyoni is a tremendous show of faith in the teenager, whose recent performances suggest that he might’ve kept his place even if Ryan Gravenberch hadn’t been missing through injury.

The heavy rotation in the forward line is quite interesting, and at least Liverpool can point to having huge strength in depth off the bench is required. If it is Barcola who starts at centre-forward, a lot of eyes will be on him to see how he fares in that unfamiliar role.

Iraola hasn’t been afraid to roll the dice, which is an ideal trait for a head coach to have. He’s made some big calls tonight, and hopefully those will pay off and our 100% record in the Champions League will be preserved going into matchday five later this month.

#2085. Erik ten Hag launches latest attack on Cristiano Ronaldo: Former Man United boss claims Portugal star's career was OVER by time he joined Juventus

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 12:32 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 14:19 EDT, 1 November 2026

Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has taken another swipe at Cristiano Ronaldo, claiming the Portugal icon's career was already over by the time he joined Juventus and eventually returned to Old Trafford.

The legendary forward's second spell at United ended acrimoniously after he launched a public attack on the club and Ten Hag, accusing the manager of 'betraying' him in a bombshell interview.

Ronaldo, whose United contract was terminated following his explosive criticism of the club, joined Al-Nassr in January 2023, while Ten Hag was eventually sacked in October 2024 after a disappointing run of results.

Last month, Ten Hag gave a wide-ranging interview to The Athletic in which he criticised Ronaldo for 'letting the team down' and accused the club's hierarchy of contributing to a 'toxic culture'.

The Dutchman has now doubled down on his criticism of the 41-year-old veteran once again, claiming Ronaldo could not 'make way' for the team.

'Every top team must embrace the top player, but the top player must also make way for the team. That was simply the problem with Ronaldo,' Ten Hag said in an interview on ESPN.

Erik ten Hag has claimed Cristiano Ronaldo's career was over by the time he returned to United

Ten Hag conducted a wide-ranging interview with The Athletic last week in which he hit out at the club's hierarchy for contributing to a 'toxic culture' - and lashed out at Ronaldo

'Let there be no misunderstanding on my part, he is of course a great player. He belongs among the greats of the world.

'But the reality is also that he hasn't been able to deliver for the last seven or eight years. From Juventus onwards, it was simply over.'

Ten Hag also praised Real Madrid, where Ronaldo statistically enjoyed the most prolific years of his career, for selling the superstar at what he believed was the perfect time.

'That is also Real Madrid's great gift,' he added. 'They see when a player is declining in level. Then they part ways at a moment when, to the outside world, they are still at their peak, but actually can no longer deliver.'

In Ten Hag's tell-all interview last month, he accused Manchester United's owners of 'breaking promises' over recruitment and blasted them for showing a lack of ambition in the transfer market.

His criticism of Manchester United came amid a turbulent spell for the club, with Lisandro Martinez and Bruno Fernandes both publicly criticising the board and manager Michael Carrick respectively in recent weeks.

Carrick was given a chance to put things right after United's chiefs met for crunch talks earlier this week in the wake of his side losing 4-1 to Como in the Champions League and 3-0 to Bournemouth in the Premier League.

According to Ten Hag, Ronaldo was not prepared to stand aside for the good of the team

Ronaldo, who now plays for Al-Nassr, is within touching distance of scoring 1,000 career goals

On Saturday, United met a similar fate as they were thumped 3-0 by Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, piling even more pressure on Carrick.

Red Devils legend Peter Schmeichel expressed his anger at Ten Hag speaking out against the club during this difficult period last week.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, former United goalkeeper Schmeichel said: 'What really annoys me in everything that has happened in the past two weeks is Ten Hag coming out and saying that he wanted Declan Rice and Harry Kane, like he was a god.

'It's so ridiculous. He brought (Lisandro) Martinez in, (Matthijs) de Ligt. I mean he brought players in that are still there, how dare he go out and say that.

'Everybody knew we should sign Harry Kane. Everyone knows we should have signed Declan Rice, that's no secret. I don't know why we didn't do that.

'But you have now people stirring the pot where they should just keep calm and not talk and maybe talk about what they did for this football club themselves, or what they didn't do.

'He wasn't a success at Manchester United. Why does he feel the need to come out and say that?

'What he's saying is "I was let down by the club" and there might be an element of truth in that but he wasn't good enough. And then he went to Bayer Leverkusen, a team who had just won the Bundesliga, and then he got sacked within, what, three games?

Ten Hag also hit out at Manchester United's hierarchy amid a turbulent time for the club

Michael Carrick has been given a chance to turn things around after chiefs held crunch talks

'Maybe just take a step back and don't put yourself in that because then you will end up with someone like me criticising him, and there's no need for that. We don't need it in the narrative.'

Ten Hag was sacked by United in October 2024 after a string of poor results left the team 14th in the Premier League.

His future had been in doubt after he led United to a disappointing eighth-placed finish in the top flight a couple of months earlier, but victory in the FA Cup final over rivals Manchester City contributed to the club's decision to give him a contract extension in the summer after crunch talks in Ibiza.

He went on to replace Xabi Alonso at Bundesliga side Bayer Leverkusen the following season, but was sacked after just three games in charge, and he criticised the club's board for this 'unprecedented' decision.

#2083. Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

United fought back after conceding an early goal against Atletico to secure their second win of pre-season.

They fell behind in the sixth minute when Arnau Ortiz’s cross into the box evaded everyone, including United keeper Tom Heaton before hitting the back of the net.

United got the equaliser their performance deserved when the impressive Shea Lacey showed his skill in the box and was fouled. From the resulting penalty, Bryan Mbeumo sent the goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

In the 72nd minute, Mbeumo got his second of the afternoon after he bundled the ball home after the United press forced Atletico into a mistake.

The Spanish side hit the post twice in the closing stages but United held on to win.

“We had a clear plan before the game, everyone stuck to it and made the game enjoyable,” Mbeumo said. “We work really hard during training for these games, the main goal is to be ready for the season starting. I have done great things on the right but also as a striker.

“I think I am more experienced on the wing but I enjoy playing as a striker. For an offensive player, it is always good to score for the team.”

United dominating possession in the opening stages with Atletico happy to sit off and let the Premier League side have it. Even in pre-season, Diego Simeone has his side set up well to defend.

The visit to the Strawberry Arena means United are back at the stadium where they won the 2017 Europa League.

📸 Wayne Rooney, 2017 🏆#UEL | @ManUtd pic.twitter.com/HxZVn1mAEQ

Gianni Infantino is facing an ultimatum from Uefa: resign or face an emergency no-confidence vote.

It is understood all 55 of Uefa’s member nations would opt to oust Infantino in a vote of no-confidence if he refuses to step down. Uefa can trigger such a vote with just 43 member nations.

European football’s governing body announced a loss of confidence on Saturday morning and has demanded change after Infantino was forced to scrap his £15bn plan to sell a stake in the World Cup.

Uefa’s statement followed widespread opposition and a revolt within Fifa’s ranks that staff are calling “kill the monster”.

The Football Association backed Uefa’s stance, saying: “We fully support Uefa’s position. It is time for a full and robust review of Fifa’s leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart.”

United: Heaton; Yoro, Maguire (c), Heaven, Shaw; Santos, Mount; Amad, Lacey, Dorgu; Mbeumo.Substitutes: Bayindir, Mee, Vitek, Amass, Armer, Kamason, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Thwaites, Gabriel, Williams, Zirkzee.

Good afternoon and welcome to pre-season coverage of Manchester United against Atletico Madrid.

Michael Carrick’s squad continue their preparations for the new season with a trip to the Swedish capital, Stockholm, where they face Diego Simeone’s La Liga side.

Last week, United cruised to a 5-0 victory over Rosenborg but today will be their first real test. They are slowly starting to get players back but the likes of captain Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans will not be involved.

“I think we’re in a good place. I think there’s four weeks to go to the start and we’re gradually getting some boys back from the World Cup as we progress,” Carrick said.

“But I think a little bit of patience and time and trying to keep ahead and as I said, keeping everyone fit but moving forward is a really good direction to go in. And as it stands right now, I think we’re in a pretty good place. So, the boys will get better as we go.”

One player who will be looking to impress is Mason Mount. He has had an injury-hit spell at Old Trafford but is fit and ready to go for the season. He is also growing into a leadership role at the club.

He told BBC Radio Manchester: “You have different types of leaders, you have ones that are very vocal. I always want to see myself as one that leads by example and never stops working on the pitch.

“I’ve been captain previously years ago. I love the role especially with a lot of younger players on the pitch being able to speak to them and make them feel comfortable in the game and off the pitch as well. It’s a role that I really like and loved having it [the captain’s armband] in the second half.”

#2082. ‘Not good’ – Ally McCoist slams Liverpool star after mistake which left teammate ‘livid’

Ally McCoist was critical of one Liverpool player for his unwitting role in Fenerbahce’s equaliser against the Reds in the first half of their Champions League game on Wednesday.

The away side took a well-deserved lead in the 25th minute when Trey Nyoni’s deflected shot sailed into the net, with the teenage midfielder being credited with his first official goal in senior football.

However, the hosts restored parity just four minutes later, and again it was with the aid of a deflection as Mason Greenwood’s free kick hit off Jeremy Jacquet and was diverted into the net, with Alisson Becker not disguising his rage at the defensive wall in front of him.

Speaking on co-commentary for TNT Sports (via BBC Sport), McCoist called out the French defender for turning his back on the ball as the set piece was struck.

The Scotsman said: “I think the goalkeeper will not be too happy with his wall. Alisson is livid. Jeremy Jacquet turns his back. You have to stand up and take it. Not good defending.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

The summer arrival from Rennes has been excellent in his time at Liverpool so far, rightly receiving plenty of praise for his performances and winning his first senior call-up for France, but he won’t be happy with his part in Greenwood’s rather fortuitous equaliser.

The normally teak-tough 21-year-old paid a heavy price for turning his back on the ball, even if nobody could legislate for the huge stroke of luck that Fenerbahce received.

He’s also met his physical match in Romelu Lukaku, with the Belgian striker standing up to Jacquet in a way that few (if any) Premier League forwards have managed since the start of this season.

If Liverpool were pegged back by a piece of brilliance which was near-impossible to defend, we’d be able to accept it, but the manner of Greenwood’s goal (and it had to be him, didn’t it?) will rankle as much with Andoni Iraola as it did with the visibly furious Alisson.

At the time of writing, hopefully the centre-back and his team can put that regrettable moment behind them and go on to take all three points home to Merseyside.

#2081. Rangers midfielder Nico Raskin desperate to end his trophy drought by lifting the Premier Sports Cup

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 14:23 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 14:23 EDT, 1 November 2026

Rangers midfielder Nico Raskin insists he is desperate to finally end his own personal trophy drought after reaching the Premier Sports Cup final.

Raskin has been at Rangers for almost four years but is yet to actually lift any silverware, something which he does not seek to shy away from.

The Belgian midfielder missed the final of this competition in December 2023 due to injury as Rangers beat Aberdeen 1-0 – and therefore did not collect a winner’s medal.

After beating the Dons by the same scoreline at Hampden last night, Rangers are now through to next month’s final against Hibs as they aim to secure the first trophy of the season.

Raskin freely admits that the fact his trophy cabinet is still bare after almost four years is something which annoys him. But it is something he is determined to rectify.

‘I just want to go and win it,’ said the 25-year-old. ‘My family tell me I’ve won one (trophy), but I tell them I haven’t.

Rangers star Nico Raskin wants to make up for missing the 2023 Premier Sports Cup final

Manager Derek McInnes joins Raskin and his Rangers team-mates after their semi-final victory

Rangers striker Ryan Naderi celebrates scoring the winner against Aberdeen at Hampden

‘When we won this competition previously, I got rested for the first two games - and injured for the next two.

‘So that’s not me winning it. Yeah (it annoys me). I think I’ve been here a long time and we’ve worked so hard.

‘Not having that is difficult, but hopefully next month we’ll win one. I’m just happy to get to this final with full belief and I want to win that cup.

‘It’s top. It’s really good for the team. But now we want to win it and there’s one game to go. Now we go full force to win the cup.’

After almost leaving Rangers at various points over the past year, Raskin insists he is now fully focused on delivering success over the rest of this campaign.

He was made captain yesterday by Derek McInnes and was glad to repay the manager’s faith with a hard-fought victory.

Despite toiling to break down a stubborn Aberdeen side, Rangers finally broke through when Ryan Naderi stabbed home from close range with only seven minutes remaining.

If Rangers can go on and lift the cup in next month’s final, Raskin believes it could pave the way for further success this season.

‘Listen, it’s not going to be an easy season. It’s a long season,’ he said. ‘But the main thing is to keep focused and keep working towards the goal.

‘We need to keep believing in the manager and what we’re doing, then we’ll be there.

‘Things happen for a reason (in terms of what happened with transfer interest) and I’m looking forward to that game next month in the final.

‘Hopefully we can achieve something good this season that will lead us to a more exciting season.

‘Aberdeen gave us a difficult game. If you think you’re going to have an easy game, coming out and winning 4-0, you’re wrong.

‘The other team is coming with a plan and it’s a big game for them, also. It’s not easy to win football games. So you go out and give the best performance you can.

‘We won, so we’re very happy. In terms of the manager, he breathes Rangers and he gives that to us.

‘It’s so good to have someone like him driving us every day and on the pitch. I’m delighted for him and hopefully we can win it for him too.

‘He told us that it wasn’t going to be easy. That if we turn up and do everything we have to do, then we’d win the game.

‘We couldn’t come out with complacency and think it would be easy to score four goals. It’s a hard game that isn’t easy to win, so we have to enjoy it when we do.’

#2080. Celtic star handed 'ideal springboard' as sensational transfer return route emerges

Carl Ikeme reckons Sam Johnstone has landed the "ideal springboard" at Celtic to revive his career, with the former Wolves goalkeeper insisting his old club can also benefit.

Johnstone was pitched straight into the heat of battle at Ibrox after his arrival, before briefly coming back out of the side. But the 33-year-old has since established himself as Celtic's clear first choice between the sticks and is beginning to put together the regular run of football he was craving after finding opportunities limited at Wolves.

And Ikeme believes playing every week at Celtic can help the former England international rediscover his best form, putting him in a position to either secure a permanent switch or return to Wolves ready to fight for the No.1 jersey.

Ikeme was speaking as part of the Midnite Express, providing luxury coach travel for 100 Wolverhampton Wanderers supporters' and said: "It simply didn't happen for him at Wolves, largely because José Sá kept the shirt and the club went through a turbulent period last season. Sam was in and out, but he’s a top goalkeeper who needs to be playing week in, week out.

Read more: Martin O'Neill fires 'a lot more' Celtic demand at £3.5m signing

"It makes no sense to have both Sam and José sitting in the same squad, especially with John Ruddy returning to provide veteran cover.

"Going to Celtic is a fantastic move. It’s a massive football club where he’ll play every week and rebuild his confidence.

"Whether he uses it to secure a permanent move or returns to challenge for the number one shirt if Wolves go up, it’s a win-win. Goalkeeping is unique: you can find yourself out of favour very quickly through no fault of your own. The crucial thing is that he’s playing regularly again.

"It's an ideal springboard. You step outside the intense Premier League goldfish bowl, even though playing for Celtic or Rangers brings immense pressure of its own.

"It allows experienced keepers to get regular minutes, find their rhythm, and compete for trophies. It’s worked brilliantly for several top keepers, and it will do the same for Sam."
